items.title: verifying identity on the phone
items.content: When you call Larkmere Mutual, we will first confirm that we are speaking with the correct person before discussing any account or policy details. We may ask you to confirm selected personal information already held on our records and, where appropriate, answer a security question. If you are unable to pass verification, we will not disclose any confidential information by telephone.

items.title: verifying identity on the phone
items.content: For your protection, our advisers must not rely on caller display, voice recognition alone, or any information provided without challenge. We may ask for more than one item of evidence to satisfy ourselves as to identity. This helps us reduce the risk of fraud and unauthorised access to member information.

items.title: verifying identity on the phone
items.content: Where a member has appointed an authorised representative, we will still complete our standard telephone security checks before dealing with the call. The representative may be asked to provide evidence of authority if that is not already recorded on the account. We will only speak to the extent permitted by that authority.

items.title: verifying identity on the phone
items.content: If you call from a number we hold on file, this does not of itself establish your identity. We may use the number as a supporting check, but we will continue with the full verification process. No change to a policy, account or claim will be made until identity has been confirmed.

items.title: verifying identity on the phone
items.content: Members should be prepared to answer questions that do not reveal their full password or memorable information in one disclosure. Our advisers may ask for selected characters, partial details or another agreed form of telephone passcode. We will never ask you to disclose your online banking credentials or full card details as a means of identification.

items.title: verifying identity on the phone
items.content: If the caller is unable to remember the required details, we may pause the conversation and arrange for an alternative method of verification. This may include a letter, secure message or other channel deemed appropriate by the Society. We will not override the process simply because a matter is urgent.

items.title: verifying identity on the phone
items.content: Where there is any doubt about impersonation, our staff must escalate the call in line with fraud prevention procedures. They may end the call and ask the member to contact us again using a published contact number. Protecting members’ information takes priority over convenience.

items.title: verifying identity on the phone
items.content: Telephone verification is required before we can quote on, amend or discuss a policy unless an exception applies under our procedures. Basic administrative information may be given only where it does not breach confidentiality. Sensitive details, including claim histories and payment information, are restricted until checks are complete.

items.title: verifying identity on the phone
items.content: If a member is calling about a joint account or joint policy, we will verify the identity of the caller before releasing any joint information. The fact that the caller is named on the account does not remove the need for security checks. Each call is assessed on its own merits and in accordance with our records.

items.title: verifying identity on the phone
items.content: Our staff are trained to keep verification questions proportionate and respectful, but they may repeat them if answers are unclear or inconsistent. Failure to verify identity may result in the call being referred to another channel or closed without action. This is part of our duty to safeguard members and their financial affairs.

items.title: verifying identity on the phone
items.content: When a member contacts us by telephone, we will first confirm their identity before discussing any account, policy or claim details. We may ask for information already held on record and will not proceed until we are satisfied that the caller is authorised to receive the information requested.

items.title: verifying identity on the phone
items.content: For security, our colleagues must never rely on a caller’s name or telephone number alone. We will use a combination of agreed verification questions and account checks before we disclose personal or financial information.

items.title: verifying identity on the phone
items.content: If a caller is unable to pass telephone verification, we will not provide account-specific assistance. In such cases, we may ask the member to call back, use a secure channel, or attend to their query through an approved alternative process.

items.title: verifying identity on the phone
items.content: We may suspend or refuse telephone access where we believe there is a heightened risk of fraud or identity theft. This is a protective measure and may remain in place until we have completed further checks.

items.title: verifying identity on the phone
items.content: Our verification questions must be answered accurately and consistently. Where responses are incomplete, contradictory or raise concern, the call should be treated as unverified and escalated in line with procedure.

items.title: verifying identity on the phone
items.content: We may ask a member to confirm recent activity, policy details or other information that only the genuine customer is likely to know. We will keep such checks proportionate and relevant to the service being requested.

items.title: verifying identity on the phone
items.content: If a member is calling on behalf of another person, we will require evidence that they are authorised to act. Telephone verification alone is not sufficient where the caller is seeking to manage another person’s policy, account or claim.

items.title: verifying identity on the phone
items.content: Where a call has been transferred internally, identity verification must still be completed if the next colleague will access sensitive information. A previous check does not remove the requirement to follow the society’s current security procedures.

items.title: verifying identity on the phone
items.content: We record the outcome of telephone identity checks for audit and security purposes. This helps us protect members, reduce fraud and demonstrate that information was only shared following appropriate verification.

items.title: verifying identity on the phone
items.content: If a member cannot complete telephone verification because of language, accessibility or other support needs, we will consider reasonable alternatives. Any alternative route must still provide a secure basis for confirming identity before information is released.

items.title: verifying identity on the phone
items.content: When a member telephones us, we must complete identity checks before discussing any account, policy or claim details. We may ask for personal information already held on record and, where needed, additional security questions. If the caller cannot be satisfactorily verified, we will not disclose confidential information.

items.title: forgotten security answers
items.content: If you have forgotten your security answer, we will not reveal or hint at the answer under any circumstances. For your protection, we may ask you to complete additional identity checks before we discuss your account.

items.title: forgotten security answers
items.content: You should not share your security answer with anyone, including a member of Larkmere Mutual staff. We will only use the answer, together with other verification checks, to confirm that we are speaking to the correct person.

items.title: forgotten security answers
items.content: Where a member cannot remember their security answer, we will help them reset it through our approved verification process. Until the reset is complete, some services may be restricted to protect the account.

items.title: forgotten security answers
items.content: Security answers are treated as confidential authentication details and must be kept separate from passwords and PINs. If you suspect that your answer may be known to another person, you must contact us without delay.

items.title: forgotten security answers
items.content: For telephone and digital servicing, a forgotten security answer may prevent us from completing your request at the first attempt. In those circumstances, we will offer an alternative method of verification where available.

items.title: forgotten security answers
items.content: We will never send a reminder of your security answer by email, text message or post. This is to reduce the risk of unauthorised access to your savings, mortgage or insurance records.

items.title: forgotten security answers
items.content: If repeated failed attempts indicate that a security answer has been forgotten or misused, we may temporarily place additional safeguards on the account. These safeguards will remain in place until identity is satisfactorily confirmed.

items.title: forgotten security answers
items.content: You may choose to reset your security answer at any time by following the instructions in your online account or by contacting us directly. Any new answer should be memorable to you, but not easy for others to guess.

items.title: forgotten security answers
items.content: For joint accounts, each authorised person must pass their own security checks before we can discuss personal information. A forgotten security answer for one person does not automatically affect the other person's access, subject to our verification rules.

items.title: forgotten security answers
items.content: If you cannot remember your security answer and do not have access to the usual verification channels, we may ask you to visit a branch or provide further evidence of identity. We will always aim to support you while keeping your account secure.

items.title: forgotten security answers
items.content: If you cannot recall your security answer, we will not disclose account details until we have completed alternative identity checks. For your protection, we may ask you to provide information from a recent policy or account interaction. We will never use a security answer as the sole means of verification where it has been forgotten.

items.title: forgotten security answers
items.content: Where a customer advises that a security answer has been forgotten, the adviser must follow the reset procedure and not attempt to guess or prompt the answer beyond the approved verification steps. The adviser should offer a secure alternative, such as a password reset or in-branch identification where available. A new answer must be set only after identity has been confirmed.

items.title: forgotten security answers
items.content: Security answers are stored in encrypted form and are not visible to staff. If the answer is forgotten, the existing answer cannot be recovered and must be replaced. Customers should be informed that this is a security control, not a fault with the service.

items.title: forgotten security answers
items.content: If you forget your security answer, you may be asked to complete additional checks before we can discuss your account. These checks are designed to protect you from unauthorised access. If we cannot satisfy ourselves as to your identity, we will not proceed.

items.title: identity documents for a new account
items.content: When opening a new account, we must confirm your identity and address before we can proceed. We will normally ask for one document from our approved list of identity documents and one document showing your current address.

items.title: identity documents for a new account
items.content: Acceptable identity documents include a valid passport, UK photocard driving licence or national identity card where applicable. Documents must be original and current unless our procedures state otherwise.

items.title: identity documents for a new account
items.content: If you are unable to provide standard identity documents, we may ask for alternative evidence. We will consider these on a case-by-case basis, but we are not obliged to accept every document presented.

items.title: identity documents for a new account
items.content: Your name on the identification provided should match the name on the application as closely as possible. If there has been a change of name, we may ask to see supporting evidence of that change.

items.title: identity documents for a new account
items.content: Proof of address must usually be dated within the last three months. Examples include a utility bill, council tax notice, bank statement or other official correspondence addressed to you at your current address.

items.title: identity documents for a new account
items.content: We do not accept screenshots, photocopies or edited images in place of original documents unless the process specifically allows it. Where copies are accepted, they must be clear, complete and capable of verification.

items.title: identity documents for a new account
items.content: Where an applicant is under 18, identity checks may be completed using alternative documents or evidence from a parent or guardian. Additional checks may be required before the account can be opened.

items.title: registering a lasting power of attorney
items.content: Where an account holder wishes a lasting power of attorney to be used, we must first receive a certified copy of the registered document or a sealed office copy. We cannot act on an unregistered lasting power of attorney unless the law permits us to do so.

items.title: registering a lasting power of attorney
items.content: We will check the attorney’s authority before allowing them to manage a member’s mortgage, savings or current account. If the lasting power of attorney is not valid, not registered where registration is required, or appears incomplete, we may be unable to accept instructions.

items.title: registering a lasting power of attorney
items.content: When a lasting power of attorney is presented, we may ask to see proof of identity for both the donor and the attorney. We may also require confirmation that the donor still has the capacity to make the request where this is relevant to the transaction.

items.title: registering a lasting power of attorney
items.content: For property and financial affairs lasting powers of attorney, registration is normally required before the attorney can act. We will only update our records once we are satisfied that the document has been properly registered and remains in force.

items.title: registering a lasting power of attorney
items.content: If a customer wants us to note a lasting power of attorney on their records, they should send us a clear copy of the registered instrument together with any reference number we ask for. We may retain copies for our records and return originals where received.

items.title: registering a lasting power of attorney
items.content: An attorney may act only within the powers granted by the lasting power of attorney and any restrictions set out in the document. We will not accept an instruction that goes beyond those powers or conflicts with any legal limitation.

items.title: registering a lasting power of attorney
items.content: Where more than one attorney is appointed, we will follow the signing arrangements shown in the lasting power of attorney. If the document requires attorneys to act jointly, we will need the agreement of all required attorneys before we can proceed.

items.title: registering a lasting power of attorney
items.content: We may place temporary restrictions on an account while we verify a lasting power of attorney. This is to protect the member and to prevent transactions being made before the appointment has been confirmed.

items.title: registering a lasting power of attorney
items.content: A lasting power of attorney does not remove the member’s rights where they still have capacity, and we will normally continue to take instructions from the member unless informed otherwise. If there is any doubt about who may give instructions, we will ask for further evidence.

items.title: registering a lasting power of attorney
items.content: Our records will show when a lasting power of attorney has been registered with us and whether it applies to one or more products. If the attorney’s details change, or the authority ends, we must be told as soon as reasonably practicable.

items.title: registering a lasting power of attorney
items.content: If you wish to act on behalf of a member under a lasting power of attorney, we must first be provided with a certified copy of the registered document. We can only accept authority once the LPA has been registered with the Office of the Public Guardian.

items.title: registering a lasting power of attorney
items.content: A lasting power of attorney must be in place and valid before we can discuss or make changes to the member's account. Where the document is not yet registered, we are unable to accept instructions from the attorney.

items.title: registering a lasting power of attorney
items.content: Please send us a copy of the registered lasting power of attorney together with any identification we request for the attorney. We will check the document and note the account once authority has been confirmed.

items.title: registering a lasting power of attorney
items.content: We may ask for the original or a certified copy of the lasting power of attorney if the copy provided is unclear or incomplete. Any certification must be current and must show the required registration details.

items.title: an attorney managing a parent's account
items.content: If you have authority to act as an attorney for a member, you may manage the account only within the scope of the power granted. We will need sight of the original or a certified copy of the lasting power of attorney, or equivalent legal authority, before we can register the arrangement. Until registration is complete, we may be unable to accept instructions from you.

items.title: an attorney managing a parent's account
items.content: An attorney must satisfy our identification and verification checks before access is granted. We may ask for evidence of your name, address and authority to act, and we may carry out additional checks where required by law. These checks are designed to protect the member and the account.

items.title: an attorney managing a parent's account
items.content: Where there is more than one attorney, we will follow the instructions set out in the legal document. If the document states that attorneys must act jointly, we will require all appointed attorneys to sign or agree as instructed. If it permits them to act independently, we may accept instructions from any one attorney acting alone.

items.title: an attorney managing a parent's account
items.content: An attorney may use the account to manage the member’s everyday banking, pay bills and make routine enquiries, subject to the powers granted. You must always act in the member’s best interests and not use the account for your own benefit unless the authority expressly permits this. We may refuse any instruction that appears inconsistent with the legal authority provided.

items.title: an attorney managing a parent's account
items.content: If a parent has mental capacity and wishes to continue dealing with the account, we will normally act on the member’s own instructions. The attorney’s authority does not usually override the member’s right to act for themselves while they remain able to do so. Where there is doubt, we may ask for further evidence or seek clarification of the legal position.

items.title: an attorney managing a parent's account
items.content: We may place restrictions on certain account features when an attorney is registered. This may include limits on new borrowing, changes to nominated payees, or requests to close products, depending on the terms of the authority and the account type. Any restriction we apply will be consistent with our legal and regulatory obligations.

items.title: an attorney managing a parent's account
items.content: An attorney must tell us promptly if the member dies, loses capacity, recovers capacity, or the power of attorney is revoked. We may suspend the attorney’s access while we review the position. This helps us ensure that only valid instructions are acted upon.

items.title: an attorney managing a parent's account
items.content: We will send account communications to the correspondence address we hold, which may be the attorney’s address if requested and appropriate. Statements, notices and other documents will be issued in line with the member’s chosen preferences and our data protection requirements. We may continue to address certain legal notices to the member where the law requires it.

items.title: an attorney managing a parent's account
items.content: An attorney is not automatically liable for the member’s debts, and acting as attorney does not make you a joint account holder. You must not mix the member’s money with your own, except where permitted for expenses paid on the member’s behalf and properly recorded. We may ask for supporting records if we need to verify how funds have been used.

items.title: an attorney managing a parent's account
items.content: If we receive conflicting instructions from the member and the attorney, we will decide how to proceed according to the authority in place and applicable law. Where necessary, we may pause transactions until the matter is resolved. We may also ask for legal advice or further evidence before taking action.

items.title: an attorney managing a parent's account
items.content: Where an account is being managed by an attorney acting under a valid power of attorney, we will need to see the original document or a certified copy before we can make any changes to the account. The attorney must act only within the authority granted by the document and in the member’s best interests.

items.title: an attorney managing a parent's account
items.content: An attorney may ask us to discuss the account, obtain statements and carry out day-to-day transactions on behalf of the donor, subject to our identity and verification checks. We may decline any instruction that falls outside the powers given or where we are not satisfied that the authority remains in force.

items.title: an attorney managing a parent's account
items.content: If the member still has mental capacity, we may continue to treat them as the account holder for any matters they choose to handle themselves. The attorney may only take over those functions that the power of attorney permits.

items.title: an attorney managing a parent's account
items.content: For a parent’s account, the attorney must provide evidence of their authority and may be asked to confirm the member’s details and current address. We will keep a note on the account that an attorney is in place and record the scope of their powers.

items.title: adding a partner to a home policy
items.content: If you wish to add a partner to your home policy, please contact us so we can update the policyholder details. We will need to confirm that your partner has an insurable interest in the home and that they normally live there. Any change may affect the premium or the terms of cover.

items.title: adding a partner to a home policy
items.content: A partner may be added to the policy as a joint policyholder where both adults share responsibility for the insurance contract. This means both policyholders are entitled to make changes and receive correspondence about the policy. We may ask for proof that you live together at the insured address.

items.title: adding a partner to a home policy
items.content: Where a partner is added to a home policy, cover will only apply from the date we accept the change. You must tell us promptly if the household composition changes, as failure to do so may affect a claim. The policy remains subject to all applicable terms, exclusions and conditions.

items.title: adding a partner to a home policy
items.content: If the home is owned or rented in one name only, a partner can still usually be added as an additional insured person if they reside at the property. However, the named policyholder remains responsible for payment of the premium unless we agree otherwise. We may request supporting documentation before confirming the amendment.

items.title: adding a partner to a home policy
items.content: When adding a partner to a buildings and contents policy, we will review whether the new arrangement alters the level of risk insured. This may include questions about occupancy, prior claims and any existing security arrangements. If the information provided is incomplete or inaccurate, we may refuse the change or adjust the cover later.

items.title: adding a partner to a home policy
items.content: A partner should be added as soon as they become a permanent resident in the home. Temporary visits do not usually require an amendment to the policy. If your partner is already named on related policies with us, you should still tell us so that records can be aligned.

items.title: adding a partner to a home policy
items.content: Adding a partner does not automatically extend cover to their separate possessions away from the home. Unless specifically included, personal possessions and accidental damage remain subject to the wording of the policy schedule. Please review the updated documents carefully once the change has been processed.

items.title: adding a partner to a home policy
items.content: For joint policyholders, any instructions to cancel, renew or make material changes to the home insurance may be accepted from either policyholder. We may nevertheless contact both parties where the change is significant. This helps us ensure the policy reflects the correct household circumstances.

items.title: adding a partner to a home policy
items.content: If your partner moves in after inception, you must notify us within a reasonable time so we can amend the policy records. We may issue revised terms showing both names if the partner is to be covered. Any revised premium will be due from the effective date of the change.

items.title: adding a partner to a home policy
items.content: We reserve the right to remove a partner from the policy if they no longer live at the insured address or if they ask to be taken off. In such cases, the policyholder should tell us immediately so that the records remain accurate. Your cover may be affected if the household details are not kept up to date.

items.title: adding a partner to a home policy
items.content: If you would like to add a partner to your home policy, we will need to update the policyholder details and confirm that the person has a financial interest in the home or contents insured. We may ask for their date of birth, contact details and whether they live at the property on a permanent basis.

items.title: adding a partner to a home policy
items.content: A partner may be added to a home policy once we have verified that the household arrangements and occupation of the property remain as declared. Any change to who lives at the property must be told to us as soon as reasonably possible.

items.title: adding a partner to a home policy
items.content: Where a partner is added to the policy, both adults are normally treated as joint policyholders unless we agree otherwise. This means each policyholder is responsible for the information given to us and for complying with the terms of cover.

items.title: adding a partner to a home policy
items.content: If your partner moves into the home after the policy has started, you must tell us before the next renewal date, and earlier where the change affects the risk we insure. Failure to notify us may affect the validity of your cover or any claim.

items.title: joint mortgage applicants
items.content: Where a mortgage is held jointly, each applicant is jointly and severally liable for the whole of the borrowing. This means we may seek repayment from either applicant for any amount outstanding under the mortgage terms.

items.title: joint mortgage applicants
items.content: All joint mortgage applicants must complete the full application process and provide evidence of identity, address and income where requested. We assess the application as a whole and do not rely on one applicant’s information alone.

items.title: joint mortgage applicants
items.content: If one joint applicant leaves the property or ceases to contribute to the repayments, the mortgage remains in force until we agree a formal change. Any variation to the parties named on the account must be approved by us in writing.

items.title: joint mortgage applicants
items.content: We will normally treat correspondence for a joint mortgage as sent to all named borrowers. One applicant may not act on behalf of the other unless we hold suitable authority and have confirmed this arrangement.

items.title: joint mortgage applicants
items.content: For affordability purposes, we consider the income, commitments and credit history of each joint applicant together. We may also take account of the relationship between applicants and the way in which the loan will be repaid.

items.title: joint mortgage applicants
items.content: Any request to add a further joint applicant or remove an existing one is subject to underwriting and legal review. We may require a new application, updated supporting documents and revised mortgage deeds before we make the change.

items.title: joint mortgage applicants
items.content: Where the mortgage is in joint names, each applicant is responsible for keeping us informed of changes in circumstance that may affect repayment. This includes changes to employment, address, relationship status or financial difficulty.

items.title: joint mortgage applicants
items.content: A payment holiday, arrears arrangement or other concession agreed with one joint borrower applies to the mortgage account as a whole. It does not remove the liability of the other borrower unless we expressly confirm otherwise.

items.title: joint mortgage applicants
items.content: If joint borrowers separate, they remain bound by the mortgage terms until the account is redeemed or restructured. We may ask both parties to agree a course of action where the legal title or occupancy of the property is changing.

items.title: joint mortgage applicants
items.content: We may need the consent of all joint mortgage applicants for certain account changes, including redemption, transfer of equity and changes to the repayment basis. Where consent is required, we will not act until the necessary documentation has been completed to our satisfaction.

items.title: joint mortgage applicants
items.content: Where a mortgage is taken out in joint names, each applicant is jointly and severally liable for the full amount owed. We may pursue either or both borrowers for any payment due under the mortgage terms.

items.title: joint mortgage applicants
items.content: All joint mortgage applicants must satisfy our lending criteria, including affordability, credit assessment and identity checks. If one applicant does not meet our requirements, we may decline the application in full.

items.title: joint mortgage applicants
items.content: Unless we agree otherwise in writing, all joint applicants must sign the mortgage offer and the legal charge. We may require each applicant to obtain independent legal advice where there is a potential conflict of interest.

items.title: joint mortgage applicants
items.content: A joint mortgage application should include the income, outgoings and commitments of each applicant. We assess the application on the combined circumstances of the applicants and the property to be mortgaged.

items.title: separating joint policyholders after a break-up
items.content: Where a joint policy is held by two policyholders who separate, the policy continues unless both parties agree an amendment or cancellation in writing, or one party can demonstrate authority to act for the other. We may require confirmation of the preferred arrangements before making any change to cover, payments or correspondence. Any alteration takes effect only from the date we process it.

items.title: separating joint policyholders after a break-up
items.content: If a joint home insurance policyholder leaves the household, the remaining policyholder may ask for the policy to be transferred into a sole name, subject to underwriting review. We will consider the details of the property occupancy, the insured interest and any change in risk before agreeing the transfer. Premiums, excesses and terms may be revised accordingly.

items.title: separating joint policyholders after a break-up
items.content: For joint current accounts and savings accounts, either account holder may ask us to discuss options after separation, but we will not remove a party without their authority or a legal instruction. Where there is a dispute, we may place restrictions on withdrawals or account changes until the position is clear. This is to protect all parties and the society.

items.title: separating joint policyholders after a break-up
items.content: A joint motor policy may be amended to reflect a change in the principal keeper or regular driver following separation. The policyholder must tell us promptly if there is any change to the vehicle’s use, where it is kept overnight, or who drives it most often. Failure to disclose these changes may affect cover or a claim outcome.

items.title: separating joint policyholders after a break-up
items.content: When joint policyholders separate, any direct debit instruction remains in force until we receive a replacement payment arrangement or a cancellation request accepted by us. We may ask for a new payer to be named where one person is no longer responsible for the policy. Missed payments may result in cancellation in line with the policy terms.

items.title: separating joint policyholders after a break-up
items.content: If the separating policyholders cannot agree who should keep the insured home or contents, we may maintain the existing joint cover temporarily while the matter is resolved. The policy must not be relied upon to settle ownership disputes. We will only act on clear written instructions or appropriate legal documents.

items.title: separating joint policyholders after a break-up
items.content: For household insurance, a request to remove one joint policyholder does not itself create cover for a new occupant or partner. Any person who will have an insurable interest or require cover must be declared and accepted by us. This includes situations where the remaining policyholder has moved address or changed their living arrangements.

items.title: changing a name after marriage
items.content: If you have changed your name following marriage, you may ask us to update your records once you have the relevant supporting documents. We will normally need evidence of the new name and a document showing the link to your previous name. Any change will apply to your policy records and correspondence once we have processed your request.

items.title: changing a name after marriage
items.content: For security, we can only amend a name after marriage when we are satisfied that the request is genuine. Please provide your marriage certificate or equivalent legal evidence together with identification in your new name if available. Where identification is not yet available, we may still update your record on production of sufficient documentary proof.

items.title: changing a name after marriage
items.content: A change of name after marriage does not alter the terms, cover, or premium of your policy. It is an administrative update only and has no effect on any existing rights or obligations under the contract. You must continue to meet all policy conditions and duties of disclosure.

items.title: changing a name after marriage
items.content: Where a policy is held jointly, we will update the name of any insured person who has changed their name after marriage once we receive the necessary evidence. The remaining policy details will stay unchanged unless you ask us to make further amendments. We may ask the policyholder to confirm the request before we proceed.

items.title: changing a name after marriage
items.content: If you have changed your name after marriage and your documents are still being updated, please contact us so that we can note the new name on your account. We may continue to use your previous name until the change has been verified. This helps us avoid delays in claims, payments and other correspondence.

items.title: changing a name after marriage
items.content: You should tell us about a change of name after marriage as soon as reasonably practicable. Delayed notification may result in letters, renewal documents or claims correspondence being issued in your former name. We are not responsible for any inconvenience caused where we have not been informed of the change.

items.title: changing a name after marriage
items.content: To change your name after marriage, we may require a copy of the marriage certificate and one form of photo identification. If the names on your documents do not match exactly, we may request additional evidence. This is to ensure that our records are accurate and secure.

items.title: changing a name after marriage
items.content: Once we have accepted evidence of your change of name after marriage, we will update the name shown on your policy schedule and related documents. Historic documents already issued under your former name will not normally be reissued unless there is a specific reason to do so. Any future documents will show your updated name.

items.title: changing a name after marriage
items.content: If your bank account name has changed after marriage, please also make sure the details held for premium refunds or claim payments are correct. We may ask for separate evidence before amending payment instructions. The society will not be liable for delays where payment details have not been updated in time.

items.title: changing a name after marriage
items.content: A request to change a name after marriage may be made by the policyholder, or by a person with authority to act on their behalf. We will only accept such requests where the individual has the proper authority and where verification checks have been completed. If we need further information, we will contact the policyholder directly.

items.title: changing a name after marriage
items.content: If you have changed your name after marriage, you must tell Larkmere Mutual as soon as reasonably practicable so that our records remain accurate. We may ask for evidence of the change, such as a marriage certificate or other official document. Once verified, we will update your policy and account details.

items.title: changing a name after marriage
items.content: A change of name after marriage does not alter the terms of your policy or your obligations under the contract. All cover continues on the basis of the information previously provided, subject to any separate change in circumstances you have notified to us. You should ensure that any payment details and correspondence names are also updated.

items.title: changing a name after marriage
items.content: Where a member changes their surname following marriage, Larkmere Mutual will amend the name shown on the policyholder record. We may retain the previous name in our internal records for audit and anti-fraud purposes. This does not affect your rights as a member or policyholder.

items.title: changing a name after marriage
items.content: You may request a name amendment by contacting us by phone, in writing or through our online service channels. We will normally complete the update once we have received satisfactory proof of the change. If the policy is jointly held, we may need confirmation from all named parties before making the amendment.

items.title: a name that doesn't match the card
items.content: If the name on the payment card does not match the name on the policy or account, we may ask for additional verification before we can process the payment. This is to protect members against unauthorised use of card details. We may also decline the payment where we cannot satisfy ourselves that the cardholder has given permission.

items.title: a name that doesn't match the card
items.content: For security reasons, we do not accept card payments from a card held in another person’s name unless we have confirmed authority to do so. Where authority is not clear, we may request that payment is made from a card in the member’s own name. This helps us reduce the risk of fraud and payment disputes.

items.title: a name that doesn't match the card
items.content: If the name entered on the card details does not exactly match the cardholder name, the payment may be referred for manual review. A mismatch does not always mean the payment will fail, but it may delay completion. We reserve the right to ask for evidence that the cardholder has consented to the transaction.

items.title: a name that doesn't match the card
items.content: Members should ensure that the cardholder name provided is correct and complete. Where the name on the card differs from the name on the policy, we may need to contact the member before proceeding. If we do not receive a satisfactory response, the transaction may be cancelled.

items.title: a name that doesn't match the card
items.content: We may accept payment by a card that is not in the policyholder’s name only where the circumstances are lawful and properly authorised. This may include a joint account or another arrangement where the cardholder has permitted use. We will not proceed if the information given is inconsistent or appears unreliable.

items.title: a name that doesn't match the card
items.content: A name mismatch on card details is treated as a risk indicator under our payment controls. In such cases, we may place the transaction on hold pending confirmation from the member. This process is designed to protect both the member and the society.

items.title: a name that doesn't match the card
items.content: Where a member submits card details with a different name, we may ask for a new card payment or an alternative method of settlement. We are unable to alter the cardholder name ourselves. Any attempt to use a card without the cardholder’s knowledge may be reported in line with our fraud procedures.

items.title: telling the society a policyholder has died
items.content: If a policyholder dies, the personal representative or next of kin should tell Larkmere Mutual as soon as reasonably practicable. We will then make the necessary changes to the account, policy or claim record in line with our bereavement procedures.

items.title: telling the society a policyholder has died
items.content: We may ask for a copy of the death certificate or an interim official record before we can discuss the policy in detail. Where probate has been granted, we may also require confirmation of the executor’s authority.

items.title: telling the society a policyholder has died
items.content: Cover under a home, motor or travel policy does not automatically end on the date of death. We will review the policy position and explain whether it can continue, be transferred, or must be cancelled.

items.title: telling the society a policyholder has died
items.content: Any direct debit, standing order or regular premium payment should be reviewed promptly after notification of death. If a payment has been taken after the date of death, we will consider whether a refund is due in accordance with our policy rules.

items.title: telling the society a policyholder has died
items.content: If the deceased was the sole policyholder, we will work with the estate’s representative to arrange cancellation or continuation where permitted. No changes will be made until we have sufficient authority to act on behalf of the estate.

items.title: telling the society a policyholder has died
items.content: For a joint policy, the surviving policyholder should contact us without delay. We will explain any change to the insured parties, payment method or correspondence details and confirm what evidence we need.

items.title: telling the society a policyholder has died
items.content: If a claim is already in progress when we are told of a death, the claim will remain open and be handled by our claims team in the usual way. We may need the executor or administrator to provide instructions before settlement can be made.

items.title: telling the society a policyholder has died
items.content: We will not issue policy documents, claim payments or other confidential information to anyone who is not properly authorised. Where there is any uncertainty, we may pause the case until we have verified the person’s authority.

items.title: telling the society a policyholder has died
items.content: Where a deceased policyholder held a savings or current account with us, the account may be restricted until we receive the appropriate legal documents. We will then explain the steps needed to close the account, transfer funds or continue operation where allowed.

items.title: telling the society a policyholder has died
items.content: We treat bereavement cases with sensitivity and aim to make the process as straightforward as possible. If the representative has difficulty providing documents, we may accept alternative evidence where this is permitted by law and our procedures.

items.title: telling the society a policyholder has died
items.content: If a policyholder dies, please tell us as soon as practicable so we can update the record and make sure the policy or account is handled correctly. We may ask for a copy of the death certificate or other evidence before we make any changes.

items.title: telling the society a policyholder has died
items.content: Where a joint policyholder has died, the remaining policyholder should contact us promptly. Cover will usually continue in force for the surviving policyholder, subject to the terms and conditions of the policy.

items.title: telling the society a policyholder has died
items.content: If the deceased was the sole named policyholder, the policy may need to be reviewed by the personal representative or executor of the estate. We will explain what steps are needed and whether cover can be maintained in the meantime.

items.title: telling the society a policyholder has died
items.content: Please notify us of a death by telephone, secure message or in writing. For data protection reasons, we may only discuss the policy with an authorised personal representative unless we have the consent of the relevant estate representative.

items.title: a claim made by the executor of an estate
items.content: Where the policyholder has died, a claim may be made by the executor or personal representative of the estate, provided we are satisfied they are acting lawfully. We may ask for a sealed copy of the grant of probate or letters of administration before we discuss the claim in detail. Until we have seen evidence of authority, we will only communicate with the appointed representative about the claim.

items.title: a claim made by the executor of an estate
items.content: An executor must provide evidence that they are entitled to act for the estate before we can settle a claim or issue payment. If more than one executor has been appointed, we may require confirmation that all executors agree to the claim instructions. We will not make payment to an individual executor unless the policy terms or the estate documents allow us to do so.

items.title: a claim made by the executor of an estate
items.content: Claims made by an executor will be handled under the policy that was in force at the time of the insured event, subject to the estate proving its authority. The death of the policyholder does not remove the need to meet the normal policy conditions, including notice of claim, evidence of loss and co-operation with our enquiries. We may ask for additional documents where ownership of the insured property or item is not clear.

items.title: a claim made by the executor of an estate
items.content: Where the claim concerns a home occupied by the deceased, the executor must tell us if the property is unoccupied, being sold or being let. This may affect the cover available, the security requirements and the steps we expect to be taken to protect the property. Failure to keep the property secure may prejudice the claim.

items.title: a claim made by the executor of an estate
items.content: For motor claims, an executor may submit the claim on behalf of the estate if the deceased was the registered keeper or owner of the vehicle. We may require the vehicle keys, V5C registration document and proof of estate authority before authorising repairs or disposal. If the vehicle is written off, any settlement will be paid to the estate unless we agree otherwise in writing.

items.title: a claim made by the executor of an estate
items.content: If a claim payment is due to the estate, we will normally pay the executor or personal representative named in the probate documents. Where the estate is subject to a solicitor’s client account, we may make payment to that account on request and on receipt of suitable authority. We will not usually divide the payment between beneficiaries.

items.title: a claim made by the executor of an estate
items.content: An executor must tell us whether the deceased had any joint policyholders, joint owners or other parties with an interest in the insured property. We may need to confirm how that interest affects the claim and who is entitled to receive any settlement. If the estate cannot establish title to the item or property claimed for, the claim may be declined.

items.title: hearing loss and phone calls
items.content: If a member has difficulty hearing over the telephone, our colleagues will offer to continue the conversation in writing, by secure message or by another suitable channel. Where needed, we may also arrange a call back at a quieter time or ask the member to use relay support. We will not treat a hearing difficulty as a reason to delay urgent assistance.

items.title: hearing loss and phone calls
items.content: When a member advises us that they have hearing loss, we will make a note on the account so that future contact is handled appropriately. This may include speaking more slowly, confirming key details in writing, and checking that the member has understood the information given. We will always seek the member's preferred way of communicating.

items.title: hearing loss and phone calls
items.content: Our telephone service is designed to be accessible, but some members may find calls difficult because of background noise, speech pace or equipment limitations. In such cases, we can switch to text-based contact without requiring a repeated explanation at every call. We will aim to reduce the need for the member to repeat personal or claim details unnecessarily.

items.title: hearing loss and phone calls
items.content: If a member cannot use the phone at all, we will provide alternative contact options for claims, account servicing and complaints. These alternatives may include secure messaging, email where appropriate, letters or face-to-face appointments where available. The absence of telephone contact will not in itself affect the member's right to make a claim or request service.

items.title: hearing loss and phone calls
items.content: Where a call is important and there is a risk that the member may not hear the full message, our colleague will summarise the main points and offer to send written confirmation. This is especially important for deadlines, settlement figures, policy changes and complaint outcomes. We will record any agreed next steps in the case file.

items.title: hearing loss and phone calls
items.content: We may ask whether a member would like to use an induction loop, hearing aid settings, or another assistive device before proceeding with a call. If the member prefers, we can speak to a named representative who has authority to act on their behalf. Any such arrangement will be made in line with data protection and consent requirements.

items.title: hearing loss and phone calls
items.content: If we are unable to make ourselves understood on a live call, our colleague will remain patient, repeat information as needed, and avoid raising their voice. We will not terminate a call solely because a member has hearing loss or requests clarification. Where communication remains difficult, the matter will be moved to a more suitable channel.

items.title: hearing loss and phone calls
items.content: For vulnerable members, including those with hearing loss, we will consider whether telephone contact is the best way to deliver sensitive information. A written explanation may be more suitable for complex topics such as claims decisions, underwriting enquiries or arrears discussions. Our aim is to communicate clearly and fairly, not simply quickly.

items.title: hearing loss and phone calls
items.content: When a member contacts us by telephone through a relay service or similar support, we will treat the conversation as we would any other customer contact. Colleagues must allow extra time and must not rush the exchange. Any necessary follow-up will be provided in a format the member can access.

items.title: hearing loss and phone calls
items.content: We expect all teams to recognise signs that a member may be struggling to hear and to respond with patience and professionalism. Training and call guidance require colleagues to pause, confirm understanding and offer accessible alternatives. This forms part of our commitment to fair treatment for all members.

items.title: hearing loss and phone calls
items.content: If a customer has hearing loss and finds telephone calls difficult, we will offer an alternative way to communicate, such as secure message, email or post. We will not insist on a telephone call where another channel is suitable for the enquiry or claim.

items.title: hearing loss and phone calls
items.content: Where a call is necessary, we will speak clearly, at a steady pace, and allow extra time for the customer to respond. We will not rush the conversation or rely on jargon that may be difficult to follow.

items.title: hearing loss and phone calls
items.content: Customers may ask us to repeat information, confirm key points in writing, or arrange a call at a quieter time of day. We will make reasonable adjustments in line with our commitment to fair and accessible service.

items.title: hearing loss and phone calls
items.content: If a customer uses a relay service or assistive technology, we will work with that method of contact wherever practicable. Staff must treat such arrangements as standard communication, not as an exception.

items.title: needing large-print or braille documents
items.content: If you need documents in large print or braille, we will provide them at no extra cost. Please tell us your preference when you contact us so we can arrange the format that best suits your needs.

items.title: needing large-print or braille documents
items.content: Larkmere Mutual is committed to making our communications accessible to all members. Where requested, we will issue policy documents, letters and claim correspondence in large print or braille as soon as reasonably practicable.

items.title: needing large-print or braille documents
items.content: You may ask for large-print or braille versions of our guidance at any time. We will record your accessibility requirement on your account so that future correspondence can be sent in the same format unless you tell us otherwise.

items.title: needing large-print or braille documents
items.content: Where a member is unable to read standard print comfortably, we will offer large-print documents as a reasonable adjustment. Braille copies can also be supplied on request, subject only to the time needed to prepare the document.

items.title: needing large-print or braille documents
items.content: Our staff must take account of accessibility needs when sending written material. If large print or braille is requested, the document must be issued promptly and in a form that is clear, legible and complete.

items.title: needing large-print or braille documents
items.content: We will not charge a fee for producing documents in large print or braille. This applies to brochures, account information, insurance documents and complaint responses.

items.title: needing large-print or braille documents
items.content: If you require correspondence in braille, please let us know whether you wish to receive all future letters in that format. We will make every reasonable effort to honour your choice across the products and services you hold with us.

items.title: sight loss and reading card numbers
items.content: If a member cannot read a card number because of sight loss, staff must not ask them to guess or rely on an unverified third party. Verify identity using the society's approved alternative checks and then continue the request in the member's preferred format.

items.title: sight loss and reading card numbers
items.content: Where a card number is needed to process a payment or enquiry, the member may provide it verbally and staff must repeat it back for confirmation. If the member prefers, they may ask a trusted person to assist, provided the member consents and the identity checks are completed.

items.title: sight loss and reading card numbers
items.content: We will not treat sight loss as a reason to delay or refuse access to a service. Our staff must offer reasonable adjustments, including reading card details aloud where appropriate and using clear, unhurried communication.

items.title: sight loss and reading card numbers
items.content: If a member is unable to read the expiry date or security code on a card due to sight loss, we should explain the information in a secure manner. Never write full card details in an unsecured format or disclose them to anyone who has not been authorised by the member.

items.title: sight loss and reading card numbers
items.content: When a member is using assistive technology, staff should allow sufficient time for the member to locate and confirm the card number. Do not interrupt, rush, or assume that the member cannot complete the task without help.

items.title: sight loss and reading card numbers
items.content: If a member reports that they can no longer read their card, we should check whether a replacement card or accessible alternative would be more suitable. The member must be supported to choose the option that best meets their needs and keeps their account secure.

items.title: sight loss and reading card numbers
items.content: Staff must be alert to the risk of fraud when card details are read out over the telephone. Before continuing, complete the society's standard verification checks and ensure that the call is private enough for the member to share sensitive information safely.

items.title: a carer speaking for a member
items.content: If a member asks a carer to speak on their behalf, we may discuss the account or policy only where we are satisfied that the member has given their clear consent. We may ask the carer to confirm the member’s name, policy number and the nature of the authority given. Where appropriate, we may record that authority on the member’s file.

items.title: a carer speaking for a member
items.content: A carer who is not the member cannot make decisions for the member unless they hold a valid power of attorney or other recognised authority. If such authority is in place, we will normally need to see evidence before we discuss sensitive information or make changes. Until then, we will treat the carer as a representative only for communication purposes.

items.title: a carer speaking for a member
items.content: Where a member is unable to speak for themselves, we will consider the carer’s request carefully and in line with our safeguarding and confidentiality requirements. We may limit the information we share if it is not necessary for the matter being handled. Our first duty is to protect the member’s interests and personal data.

items.title: a carer speaking for a member
items.content: A carer may help a member by explaining their circumstances, asking questions and relaying information. However, the member remains responsible for any instruction given unless we have recognised legal authority to act otherwise. We may ask to speak directly with the member where this is possible and appropriate.

items.title: a carer speaking for a member
items.content: When a carer contacts us, we will verify their identity and relationship to the member before proceeding. We may ask whether the member is aware of the contact and whether they have agreed to the discussion. If there is any doubt, we will pause the conversation until consent or authority is established.

items.title: a carer speaking for a member
items.content: We will make reasonable adjustments where a member needs a carer to assist with communication because of age, illness or disability. Such assistance does not of itself give the carer the right to receive full account details or to amend the member’s arrangements. Any access beyond ordinary support must be authorised in advance or supported by legal documentation.

items.title: a carer speaking for a member
items.content: If a carer reports a complaint, claim or change of circumstances, we may accept the information provisionally while we confirm the member’s wishes. We will not treat the carer’s statement as binding unless the member has authorised them to act for that purpose. Where necessary, we may contact the member separately to verify the instruction.

items.title: a carer speaking for a member
items.content: We may correspond with a carer on behalf of a member where the member has asked us to do so. This may include letters, secure messages or telephone contact, depending on the member’s preference and the nature of the matter. We will continue to address the member as our customer and principal contact unless instructed otherwise.

items.title: a carer speaking for a member
items.content: A carer must not request a payment, change of beneficiary or cancellation of cover unless they have the proper authority to do so. If they do not, we will decline the request and explain what evidence is required. For the avoidance of doubt, informal care arrangements are not enough on their own.

items.title: a carer speaking for a member
items.content: Where a member’s condition or circumstances change, we may ask the carer to help us maintain accurate records of their support needs. We will use that information only for the purpose for which it was provided. All information shared by a carer is handled in accordance with our confidentiality and data protection obligations.

items.title: a carer speaking for a member
items.content: Where a member asks a carer to speak on their behalf, we will normally deal with the carer only after the member has given clear permission. We may ask the member to confirm this by telephone, secure message or in writing before discussing their account or policy.

items.title: a carer speaking for a member
items.content: A carer may help a member complete forms, make enquiries and understand our communications. However, the member remains responsible for any decision made under the account or policy, unless a valid power of attorney or similar legal authority has been registered with us.

items.title: a carer speaking for a member
items.content: We will always seek to support members who need assistance because of illness, disability or frailty. If a carer is acting for the member, we may ask questions to satisfy ourselves that the arrangement is in the member’s best interests and that the member understands what is being agreed.

items.title: a carer speaking for a member
items.content: If a carer contacts us about a claim, we may discuss general progress and request documents where the member has authorised this. We will not disclose sensitive personal information unless we are satisfied that the member has consented or there is another lawful basis for doing so.

items.title: a member in hospital during a claim
items.content: If a member is admitted to hospital during the progress of a claim, we will note the claim file and pause any time-limited request for information where it is reasonable to do so. We may contact the member later, or their nominated representative, once they are able to respond.

items.title: a member in hospital during a claim
items.content: Where a member is in hospital, we may accept a report from a spouse, partner, family member or other authorised person to help us continue handling the claim. We will only rely on such information to the extent that it is relevant and can be verified.

items.title: a member in hospital during a claim
items.content: If hospital treatment prevents a member from signing forms, giving instructions or completing a statement, we will allow additional time. We may ask for confirmation from the hospital, where appropriate, before extending deadlines or making any exception to normal process.

items.title: a member in hospital during a claim
items.content: A member’s absence due to hospitalisation does not of itself affect cover, provided the policy terms continue to be met. Claims will continue to be assessed on the evidence available and in accordance with the policy wording.

items.title: a member in hospital during a claim
items.content: Where a claim requires urgent decisions, we will seek to speak to the member as soon as practicable after hospital admission. If this is not possible, we will keep a clear record of the decision-making carried out and the reasons for it.

items.title: a member in hospital during a claim
items.content: If a member is unable to manage repairs, replacement or emergency mitigation because they are in hospital, we may arrange for a contractor or third party to act on their behalf with authority. Any such arrangement must be limited to the claim and approved by us.

items.title: a member in hospital during a claim
items.content: We will not assume that hospital admission means a member lacks capacity. Where there is concern about capacity, we will deal with the matter sensitively and may request appropriate evidence or authority before proceeding on another person’s instructions.

items.title: struggling to pay the mortgage
items.content: If you are struggling to keep up with your mortgage payments, please contact us as soon as possible. The earlier you speak to us, the more options we may have to help you manage the situation.

items.title: struggling to pay the mortgage
items.content: We will always treat customers in financial difficulty with fairness and understanding. Our first step is to review your circumstances and discuss whether a temporary arrangement may be suitable.

items.title: struggling to pay the mortgage
items.content: You may be able to reduce your monthly payments by changing the way your mortgage is repaid, extending the term, or moving to a different payment arrangement. Any change will depend on your individual circumstances and the terms of your mortgage.

items.title: struggling to pay the mortgage
items.content: If you have missed a payment, or think you may miss one, do not ignore the problem. Contact us promptly so that we can consider the support available and explain any likely consequences if the arrears continue.

items.title: struggling to pay the mortgage
items.content: Where a customer is experiencing temporary difficulty, we may agree a short-term payment plan. This is intended to help you get back on track while keeping your account under review.

items.title: struggling to pay the mortgage
items.content: We may ask you for information about your income, outgoings and any changes to your household circumstances. This helps us assess what support may be appropriate and whether the difficulty is likely to be short term or longer lasting.

items.title: struggling to pay the mortgage
items.content: If you are receiving benefits, have had a reduction in household income, or are affected by illness, separation or redundancy, please tell us. These matters can affect the options we can consider and the speed of the decision we make.

items.title: struggling to pay the mortgage
items.content: Interest may continue to be charged on arrears in line with your mortgage terms. We will explain this clearly before any arrangement is put in place and will keep you informed if your account remains in arrears.

items.title: struggling to pay the mortgage
items.content: If we cannot reach agreement with you, or if arrears build up, further action may be considered in accordance with our mortgage conditions and legal obligations. We would rather work with you early than have to take that step.

items.title: struggling to pay the mortgage
items.content: You may wish to obtain free independent debt advice if you are worried about your wider finances. We can signpost you to organisations that may help you understand your options and prioritise your commitments.

items.title: struggling to pay the mortgage
items.content: If you are worried about making your monthly mortgage payment, please contact us as soon as possible. The earlier you speak to us, the more options we may be able to discuss with you.

items.title: struggling to pay the mortgage
items.content: We will treat every request for help with understanding and fairness. Our aim is to agree a solution that reflects your circumstances and helps you keep your home wherever possible.

items.title: struggling to pay the mortgage
items.content: You should tell us if your income has fallen, your costs have risen, or you have experienced a life event such as illness, redundancy or separation. We may ask for information about your finances so we can consider suitable support.

items.title: struggling to pay the mortgage
items.content: Depending on your situation, we may be able to offer a temporary payment arrangement, a change to your payment date, or a review of your mortgage term. Any arrangement we agree will be confirmed to you in writing.

items.title: struggling to pay the mortgage
items.content: Missing a mortgage payment may mean you pay additional interest and charges. It can also affect your credit record and reduce the options available to you later.

items.title: struggling to pay the mortgage
items.content: We will never ask you to leave the property without first considering all reasonable steps to help you resolve the arrears. However, if payments continue to be missed, we may take further action in line with our legal and regulatory obligations.

items.title: struggling to pay the mortgage
items.content: If you receive a payment holiday or reduced payment arrangement, this may not remove the amount you owe. The missed or reduced payments may be added to the balance and will usually increase the total cost of the mortgage.

items.title: struggling to pay the mortgage
items.content: Where appropriate, we may signpost you to free independent money guidance and debt advice. This can help you review your household budget and identify any wider support that may be available.

items.title: struggling to pay the mortgage
items.content: If your mortgage is secured on your home, we may ask you to complete an income and expenditure assessment. This helps us understand what you can afford and what options are sustainable for you.

items.title: struggling to pay the mortgage
items.content: We will keep a record of any vulnerability or hardship information you share with us. This allows us to handle your case with appropriate care and to avoid asking you to repeat details unnecessarily.

items.title: struggling to pay the mortgage
items.content: If you are worried about making your mortgage payment, please contact us as soon as possible. We may be able to discuss a temporary arrangement to help you manage your account.

items.title: asking to pay a premium monthly instead
items.content: If you ask to pay your premium monthly, we may be able to change your payment plan subject to affordability checks and our underwriting criteria. Monthly payment is an alternative to paying the full premium upfront and may increase the total amount you pay over the year.

items.title: asking to pay a premium monthly instead
items.content: Where monthly instalments are available, we will confirm the amount of each payment and the dates on which they will be taken. You must keep enough money in your account for each collection to avoid a missed payment.

items.title: asking to pay a premium monthly instead
items.content: If you move from annual to monthly payments, any adjustment to your premium will be shown on your revised schedule. The change will only take effect once we have confirmed acceptance of your request.

items.title: asking to pay a premium monthly instead
items.content: Monthly payment may not be available for every product or customer. We may refuse a request where the payment method is unsuitable or where there is an existing arrears balance on the policy.

items.title: asking to pay a premium monthly instead
items.content: If a monthly payment is missed, we may retry collection or contact you to arrange immediate payment. Continued non-payment may lead to cancellation of cover in line with the policy terms.

items.title: asking to pay a premium monthly instead
items.content: You can usually ask to pay monthly at renewal or when you first take out a policy. If your request is accepted, we will issue updated documents showing the payment plan and any applicable finance charges.

items.title: asking to pay a premium monthly instead
items.content: Paying monthly is a regulated credit arrangement on some products and may involve interest or administrative charges. We will tell you the cost before you agree to the arrangement.

items.title: asking to pay a premium monthly instead
items.content: If you change your mind after switching to monthly payments, you may ask to return to annual payment at the next available opportunity. Any outstanding instalments must still be paid in full.

items.title: asking to pay a premium monthly instead
items.content: We may require the first monthly payment to be taken before cover is confirmed or renewed. If that first payment is not successful, the request to pay monthly may be withdrawn.

items.title: asking to pay a premium monthly instead
items.content: Where a member is experiencing financial difficulty, we will consider reasonable payment options, which may include monthly instalments. We will treat such requests sympathetically and in accordance with our collections procedure.

items.title: asking to pay a premium monthly instead
items.content: If you wish to pay your premium monthly instead of in one lump sum, we may be able to offer this subject to acceptance and affordability checks. Monthly payment is a payment arrangement and is not available on all products.

items.title: asking to pay a premium monthly instead
items.content: You should ask for monthly payment before your policy begins or as soon as you know your circumstances have changed. Once a policy has started, a change to monthly instalments may not be possible until renewal.

items.title: asking to pay a premium monthly instead
items.content: Where monthly payment is available, the total amount you pay over the year may be higher than if you pay the premium in full. Any applicable interest or instalment charge will be shown before you agree to proceed.

items.title: asking to pay a premium monthly instead
items.content: To switch to monthly payment, we may ask you to confirm your bank details and complete a direct debit instruction. Your first instalment may include an initial amount to keep the account in step with your cover start date.

items.title: illness affecting income
items.content: If illness reduces your household income, you should contact us as soon as possible so we can discuss the support available. We may ask for evidence of the change in circumstances, such as medical or employment documentation. Any arrangement we agree will depend on your individual circumstances and our assessment at the time.

items.title: illness affecting income
items.content: Where an illness means you cannot maintain your mortgage payments in full, we will consider options to help you avoid arrears. These may include a temporary payment arrangement, a change to the payment date or a review of the term. We will explain any consequences before agreeing a change.

items.title: illness affecting income
items.content: If you are unable to work because of illness, you must tell us promptly if your income protection, sick pay or other expected income changes. Delays in notifying us may affect the support we can offer. We will always deal with your case sensitively and in line with your circumstances.

items.title: illness affecting income
items.content: For current account customers, illness affecting income may lead to reduced balances or missed payments. We may be able to help by discussing short-term breathing space or by reviewing regular commitments. You remain responsible for keeping us informed of any significant change in your ability to pay.

items.title: illness affecting income
items.content: When assessing requests linked to illness, we will take account of your whole financial position, including essential household spending and any benefits received. We may ask you to complete an income and expenditure review. This helps us identify a sustainable arrangement and avoid further difficulty.

items.title: illness affecting income
items.content: If illness is likely to last for more than a short period, we may recommend that you seek independent debt advice. We will not make assumptions about your condition or recovery. Our aim is to work with you fairly and to support you in maintaining your commitments where possible.

items.title: illness affecting income
items.content: Any payment concession agreed because of illness is usually temporary. You may be required to resume your original payments once your circumstances improve. If you cannot do so, you should contact us before the concession ends so we can review the position.

items.title: illness affecting income
items.content: In cases where illness has reduced your income and you are insured with us, you should check whether your policy includes protection for sickness or incapacity. Claims under such cover are subject to the relevant policy terms, waiting periods and exclusions. We will explain what evidence is needed to assess the claim.

items.title: illness affecting income
items.content: We may ask for confirmation from a medical professional or employer where illness is said to affect income. Any information we request will be limited to what is reasonably necessary to assess your case. We will handle all personal and health information in accordance with our privacy obligations.

items.title: illness affecting income
items.content: If you are worried that illness may stop you meeting future payments, do not wait until the account is in arrears.
