Early contact gives us more opportunity to help and may prevent additional charges or further action. We will treat you with respect and review your situation without unreasonable delay.

items.title: illness affecting income
items.content: If illness means you cannot work, you should tell us as soon as reasonably possible and keep us updated on any change in your circumstances. We may ask for evidence from your employer, GP or other treating clinician to support your request for help.

items.title: illness affecting income
items.content: Where illness reduces your household income, we will consider temporary arrangements to help you maintain your policy, account or mortgage commitments. Any arrangement we agree will depend on your circumstances and may be reviewed at regular intervals.

items.title: illness affecting income
items.content: You must continue to pay any amount that is not covered by an agreed payment arrangement. If you do not keep to the terms we set out, your account may fall into arrears and further action may follow.

items.title: illness affecting income
items.content: For income protection claims, payment is based on the cover selected and the medical evidence provided. We will assess whether the illness prevents you from carrying out your occupation in the way described in your policy wording.

items.title: moving home mid-policy
items.content: If you move home during the policy term, you must tell us as soon as reasonably possible. We will update your records and confirm whether the cover can continue at your new address or whether a change to the terms is needed.

items.title: moving home mid-policy
items.content: Your insurance is arranged for the home shown on your schedule. Cover may not automatically transfer to a different property, even where the move is within the United Kingdom.

items.title: moving home mid-policy
items.content: Before completion of your move, you must tell us the date you expect to leave your current home and the date you expect to occupy the new one. This helps us make sure the correct property is insured at the correct time.

items.title: moving home mid-policy
items.content: Where there is a period when neither property is occupied by you, different terms may apply. We may ask questions about security, contents, and any works planned at either address.

items.title: moving home mid-policy
items.content: If you are buying a new home and selling your current one, we may be able to note both addresses for a limited time. Any such arrangement must be agreed by us in advance and will be subject to the terms we set out in writing.

items.title: moving home mid-policy
items.content: Any premium adjustment arising from a move home will be based on the details of the new property and the risk we assess. If the new address is not acceptable to us, we may cancel the policy in accordance with its terms.

items.title: moving home mid-policy
items.content: You must ensure that the sums insured remain adequate after you move. A larger home, different construction, or a higher rebuild cost may mean your existing cover is no longer sufficient.

items.title: moving home mid-policy
items.content: If you change address and do not tell us, a claim may be affected. We may reduce, refuse or adjust a claim where the information we hold is no longer correct and that affects the cover provided.

items.title: moving home mid-policy
items.content: Where the new home is still being completed or is not yet ready for occupation, you must tell us immediately. We will tell you whether we can insure it, and from what date any cover will start.

items.title: moving home mid-policy
items.content: Any no claims or claims history on the policy will usually remain with you when you move, subject to our underwriting rules. However, moving to a different property type or location may change the terms available to you.

items.title: moving home mid-policy
items.content: If you move home during the policy term, you must tell us as soon as possible so we can update the insured address and any related cover details. Your premium may change from the date of the move, depending on the risk at the new property.

items.title: moving home mid-policy
items.content: Cover for your previous home may end when you no longer have an insurable interest in it, unless we agree otherwise in writing. You should not assume both properties are covered at the same time.

items.title: moving home mid-policy
items.content: Where you are moving to a property that is not yet occupied, you must tell us whether the home will be empty, furnished or occupied on completion. Different conditions and security requirements may apply to an unoccupied property.

items.title: moving home mid-policy
items.content: If the new home is in Scotland, Northern Ireland or outside the United Kingdom, this policy will not continue automatically. You must contact us before completion to check whether we can offer cover.

items.title: moving home mid-policy
items.content: Any claim arising after the move will be assessed against the details we hold for the new address, not the previous one. Failure to notify us promptly may affect your cover or the amount we pay.

items.title: moving home mid-policy
items.content: If you are purchasing a new home and selling your previous one, you must tell us which address is your main residence from the date of completion. We may ask for the completion date and other conveyancing details to confirm the change.

items.title: moving home mid-policy
items.content: When you move, any optional sections, endorsements or agreed limits that apply to your former home do not automatically transfer. We may need to reassess valuables, accidental damage, and any security conditions for the new property.

items.title: moving home mid-policy
items.content: If the new home has a different construction type, rebuild cost, roof material or alarm arrangement, you must disclose this before the move is completed. These changes may affect both acceptance and price.

items.title: moving home mid-policy
items.content: You must take reasonable steps to protect the property during the move, including removing valuables and securing doors and windows. Loss or damage caused by failure to secure the property may not be covered.

items.title: moving home mid-policy
items.content: Where we agree to continue cover at the new address, we will confirm the revised premium and policy schedule in writing. The updated documents will replace the previous schedule from the effective date shown.

items.title: moving home mid-policy
items.content: If your insured home changes because you are moving house, you must tell us as soon as possible and before the move date if you can. We will confirm whether cover can continue at the new address and whether any changes to premium or terms are needed.

items.title: porting a mortgage to a new property
items.content: If you wish to move your mortgage to a new property, you must first make a formal porting application and provide details of the property you intend to buy. Porting is subject to affordability, underwriting and the property meeting our lending criteria. We may need to review the term, loan amount or repayment basis before giving approval.

items.title: porting a mortgage to a new property
items.content: A mortgage may only be ported where the existing account is up to date and no material breach of the mortgage conditions has occurred. Any arrears or unresolved account issues may prevent the transfer from proceeding. We will confirm in writing whether the mortgage can be ported to the new property.

items.title: porting a mortgage to a new property
items.content: Porting does not guarantee that the full existing loan will be available on the new property. If the new borrowing required is greater than the balance being transferred, the additional amount will be treated as new lending and assessed separately. This may result in a different interest rate or product terms for the extra borrowing.

items.title: porting a mortgage to a new property
items.content: When a mortgage is ported, the original property must normally be sold or otherwise redeemed in accordance with the porting timetable we agree with you. If the sale does not complete within the required period, the existing mortgage may need to be repaid in full. We may charge separate fees for the redemption and completion of the new mortgage.

items.title: porting a mortgage to a new property
items.content: Our agreement to port a mortgage is conditional upon valuation of the new property and, where applicable, a satisfactory survey. We may decline the application if the property type, condition or construction falls outside our lending policy. Any decision will be based on the information available at the time of assessment.

items.title: porting a mortgage to a new property
items.content: If you hold a fixed or discounted rate, portability may be available only within the product terms and any applicable time limits. Early repayment charges may still apply to part or all of the existing loan unless the product conditions provide otherwise. You should check the key facts illustration and your mortgage offer before making plans to move.

items.title: porting a mortgage to a new property
items.content: Where a mortgage is ported jointly, all borrowers named on the original account must usually remain party to the new mortgage unless we agree otherwise. Any change in borrowers will require a separate application and may affect the porting decision. We may ask for updated identification and income evidence from each applicant.

items.title: porting a mortgage to a new property
items.content: Porting is not available where the new property is intended for business use or for letting, unless the mortgage product specifically permits this. The new property must ordinarily be used as your main residence. We reserve the right to refuse porting where the intended use is inconsistent with the original lending basis.

items.title: porting a mortgage to a new property
items.content: If the new property is in a higher risk location or otherwise presents a different lending risk, we may impose conditions or reduce the amount we are willing to lend. These conditions may include a lower loan-to-value ratio, additional documentation or revised affordability checks. Our decision will reflect both the property risk and your ability to meet the new payments.

items.title: porting a mortgage to a new property
items.content: You remain responsible for keeping both the old and new mortgage arrangements within the agreed timescales during the porting process. Failure to complete the sale and purchase in time may mean the porting offer is withdrawn. In that event, the existing mortgage terms will continue until redeemed or replaced in accordance with the mortgage conditions.

items.title: porting a mortgage to a new property
items.content: A mortgage may be ported to a new property, subject to the Society’s current lending criteria at the time of application. Porting is not automatic and must be approved before any existing borrowing is transferred.

items.title: porting a mortgage to a new property
items.content: When you ask to port your mortgage, we will assess the new property as a fresh lending case. This includes checking affordability, the value and condition of the property, and whether the property is suitable security for the loan.

items.title: porting a mortgage to a new property
items.content: If the new property is worth less than the amount outstanding on your current mortgage, you may need to make up the difference. Any additional borrowing will be treated as new lending and may be offered on different terms.

items.title: porting a mortgage to a new property
items.content: A porting request should be made as early as possible, and before you exchange contracts on the sale or purchase. We cannot guarantee approval, and you should not rely on portability until the Society has confirmed acceptance in writing.

items.title: a gap between selling and buying
items.content: Where a member sells a property and is temporarily without another home to insure, cover may continue only if the policy terms permit an unoccupied period. Members must tell us at once if the home becomes empty, as different terms, conditions and security requirements may apply.

items.title: a gap between selling and buying
items.content: If there is a gap between exchange, completion and moving in, the member must ensure the existing policy remains in force until responsibility for the new property begins. Larkmere Mutual will not assume cover for a property that has been sold unless it is specifically noted on the policy schedule.

items.title: a gap between selling and buying
items.content: For mortgage arrangements, a break between selling one property and buying another does not alter the member’s duty to make payments when due. Any request for payment holiday, change of direct debit date or temporary support must be agreed in advance and confirmed by us in writing.

items.title: a gap between selling and buying
items.content: When a member has sold a home but the new home is not yet ready for occupation, they must take reasonable steps to protect any insured property and belongings. This includes keeping doors and windows secured, attending the property regularly where required, and removing valuables if the premises will be left vacant.

items.title: a gap between selling and buying
items.content: If a member expects a gap between moving out and moving in, they should arrange suitable insurance for each stage of the move. Standard home insurance may not provide full cover for goods in transit, temporary storage or a vacant property, unless the policy wording says otherwise.

items.title: a gap between selling and buying
items.content: A short gap between selling and buying may affect buildings cover on the day of completion. The member is responsible for checking the exact time at which risk passes under the contract and for ensuring that insurance begins and ends at the correct point.

items.title: a gap between selling and buying
items.content: Where a property is unoccupied during a gap in residence, we may require us to be notified after 30 consecutive days emptying, or sooner if the policy says so. Failure to notify us may result in reduced cover or a claim being declined in accordance with the policy terms.

items.title: rebuild cost after an extension
items.content: If you add an extension, you must tell us as soon as the work is complete or sooner if the rebuild cost may change materially. We may ask for an updated rebuilding valuation so that your buildings sum insured remains adequate.

items.title: rebuild cost after an extension
items.content: The rebuild cost must reflect the full cost of reinstating the home to the same standard, including the extension, not the market value. It should allow for professional fees, labour, materials and site clearance where applicable.

items.title: rebuild cost after an extension
items.content: Where an extension increases the size or complexity of the property, the original sum insured may no longer be sufficient. If the amount insured is too low, any claim settlement may be reduced in line with the underinsurance clause.

items.title: rebuild cost after an extension
items.content: Temporary works, planning conditions and the cost of complying with current building regulations may affect the rebuild cost after an extension. You should take these into account when reviewing your cover.

items.title: rebuild cost after an extension
items.content: A loft conversion, conservatory or other structural extension can increase the total rebuilding expense even if the floor area change is modest. We therefore recommend a fresh assessment rather than relying on the previous figure.

items.title: rebuild cost after an extension
items.content: You are responsible for ensuring the buildings sum insured is kept up to date after alterations to the property. Failure to report an extension may affect the level of cover available for the rebuilt structure and any attached fixtures.

items.title: rebuild cost after an extension
items.content: If an extension changes the construction materials or roof type, the rebuild cost may rise by more than the visible increase in size alone. Our underwriting review will consider the revised specification of the whole building.

items.title: rebuild cost after an extension
items.content: Any estimate of rebuild cost should include the cost of demolishing unsafe remains and rebuilding the property from the ground up after a total loss. An extension must be included in that estimate even where it is newly built or only partially finished.

items.title: rebuild cost after an extension
items.content: We may use indexation as a guide between reviews, but index-linking does not replace an updated rebuild assessment after significant alterations. An extension is treated as a change that may require immediate adjustment to the insured amount.

items.title: rebuild cost after an extension
items.content: If you are unsure whether an extension has changed the rebuild cost, you should seek a professional rebuilding valuation without delay. Keeping the figure accurate helps avoid a shortfall at claim stage and supports fair settlement of any insured loss.

items.title: rebuild cost after an extension
items.content: If you add an extension, you must tell us as soon as the work is complete and before any future claim. The rebuild cost of the home will usually increase, and your buildings sum insured should be reviewed to reflect the extra area and any higher reinstatement costs.

items.title: rebuild cost after an extension
items.content: Our buildings cover is based on the full cost of rebuilding the property, not its market value. An extension may change the rebuild cost, so the amount insured should be checked after completion and whenever further alterations are made.

items.title: rebuild cost after an extension
items.content: Where an extension has been built, the rebuild cost must include the additional floor area, foundations, walls, roof, fittings and any increased professional fees. If these changes are not taken into account, the sum insured may be insufficient for a claim.

items.title: rebuild cost after an extension
items.content: You should obtain an updated rebuild cost whenever an extension alters the structure or materials of the home. The assessment should consider demolition, site clearance, labour, materials and compliance with current building requirements.

items.title: a listed or older building
items.content: If your home is a listed building, you must tell us before we issue or renew cover. We will only insure it on the basis that any repair, reinstatement or alteration complies with all statutory consents and conservation requirements.

items.title: a listed or older building
items.content: For older properties, we may ask for construction details, roof type, and any previous structural work before confirming cover. Where the property has been substantially altered, we may treat it as non-standard for underwriting purposes.

items.title: a listed or older building
items.content: You must obtain all necessary consent before carrying out repair works to a listed building. We will not pay for any additional cost arising from failure to obtain approval from the relevant public authority or local planning body.

items.title: a listed or older building
items.content: Where a claim concerns an older property, we may repair using suitable modern materials if the original materials are no longer available. We will aim to preserve the character of the building where this is reasonably practicable and consistent with the policy terms.

items.title: a listed or older building
items.content: If the building is listed, the most appropriate repair method may cost more than a standard reinstatement. Subject to the policy limit and any endorsement, we will consider reasonable extra costs that are necessary to meet conservation obligations.

items.title: a listed or older building
items.content: Routine maintenance remains your responsibility, particularly where age-related wear and tear is evident. We do not cover damage that arises gradually from deterioration, rot, corrosion or defective workmanship, whether the property is listed or not.

items.title: a listed or older building
items.content: Where an older building has single-skin walls, timber framing or lime plaster, you must maintain it in a suitable condition for its construction type. Failure to carry out regular upkeep may affect any claim if the loss is linked to neglect or pre-existing defect.

items.title: insuring a holiday cottage
items.content: A holiday cottage must be disclosed to us as a property used for short-stay letting or occasional guest occupation. Standard home insurance may not provide the cover required where the property is let, unoccupied for extended periods, or managed by third parties.

items.title: insuring a holiday cottage
items.content: We will ask whether the cottage is occupied by the policyholder, family members, paying guests, or a mixture of these uses. The answers we receive may affect the premium, the terms applied, and whether certain sections of cover are available.

items.title: insuring a holiday cottage
items.content: Where a holiday cottage is left empty between lets, the unoccupancy condition in the policy will still apply. You must make sure all locks, alarms, and frost precautions are in use, and any inspection requirement in the schedule is followed.

items.title: insuring a holiday cottage
items.content: Buildings cover for a holiday cottage is intended to protect the structure, outbuildings, fixtures, and fittings against insured events. Contents cover, where selected, applies only to items owned by the policyholder and kept at the insured address, subject to the limits and exclusions shown in the wording.

items.title: insuring a holiday cottage
items.content: If the cottage is advertised or let through an agency or booking platform, you must tell us the full arrangement. Failure to disclose commercial letting activity may result in a claim being reduced, declined, or the policy being cancelled.

items.title: insuring a holiday cottage
items.content: We do not expect the insured property to be used as a permanent residence if it is insured as a holiday cottage. If the use changes, including a move to long-term tenancy or owner occupation, you must notify us without delay.

items.title: insuring a holiday cottage
items.content: Escape of water is a common cause of loss in properties that stand empty for periods. For holiday cottages, you should ensure the heating system is maintained and any water system precautions required by the policy are followed during cold weather or between guest stays.

items.title: a buy-to-let flat
items.content: A buy-to-let flat may be insured under a landlord arrangement provided it is occupied under a formal tenancy agreement. The policyholder must tell us if the property is let to family, friends or a company, as different terms may apply.

items.title: a buy-to-let flat
items.content: Where a flat is held on a leasehold basis, the policyholder remains responsible for checking that the lease permits letting. We may ask to see evidence of consent from the freeholder or managing agent if this is required by the lease.

items.title: a buy-to-let flat
items.content: The insured flat must be maintained in a good state of repair and kept secure when unoccupied. Failure to fit approved locks, work smoke alarms or arrange appropriate visits during long absences may affect cover.

items.title: a buy-to-let flat
items.content: We do not cover damage caused by gradual wear and tear, poor maintenance or condensation in a buy-to-let flat. Losses arising from a long-standing leak, defective grouting or repeated damp are not treated as sudden insured events.

items.title: a buy-to-let flat
items.content: If the flat is left empty for more than the period shown in the schedule, additional terms may apply. During any unoccupancy, the policyholder must take reasonable steps to drain down systems, remove valuables and inspect the premises regularly.

items.title: a buy-to-let flat
items.content: Damage caused by escape of water from fixed plumbing, heating systems or domestic appliances may be covered, subject to the terms and limits of the policy. However, the policyholder must act promptly to stop the leak and prevent further loss.

items.title: a buy-to-let flat
items.content: The policy does not insure loss of rent unless that cover has been specifically selected and shown on the schedule. Where rent protection applies, the insured event must make the flat uninhabitable or otherwise meet the stated trigger conditions.

items.title: a buy-to-let flat
items.content: Any alteration to the flat, including loft conversion, removal of internal walls or installation of a fitted kitchen, must be reported before the works begin. We may revise the terms, excess or premium where the construction or risk profile has changed.

items.title: a buy-to-let flat
items.content: Contents belonging to tenants are not covered unless tenant contents cover has been purchased. The landlord should make clear, in the tenancy paperwork, which items remain the tenant's responsibility and which are insured by us.

items.title: a buy-to-let flat
items.content: In the event of a claim, the policyholder must provide proof of ownership, tenancy and any repair invoices we reasonably request. We may appoint our own surveyor or loss adjuster to assess the cause of damage and the appropriate remedy.

items.title: a buy-to-let flat
items.content: A buy-to-let flat must be occupied only by tenants under a written tenancy agreement and not used as a holiday let, Airbnb-style short-term accommodation, or for any business activity that increases the risk to the property. The policy holder must tell us if the flat is left unoccupied for more than 30 consecutive days.

items.title: a buy-to-let flat
items.content: Where a flat is let to tenants, the buildings cover applies to the interest insured as stated in the schedule and is subject to the landlord’s duty to keep the property in a good state of repair. We may decline or reduce a claim where disrepair, wear and tear, or a failure to carry out reasonable maintenance has contributed to the loss.

items.title: a buy-to-let flat
items.content: A buy-to-let flat must form part of a residential block and must not be used for mixed commercial purposes unless we have agreed this in writing. Any conversion, internal alteration, or removal of load-bearing structure must be notified to us before the work begins.

items.title: a buy-to-let flat
items.content: The insured must keep the flat fitted with working smoke alarms in accordance with legal requirements and must arrange that any gas and electrical installations are maintained safely. We may ask for evidence of inspection or servicing where a claim arises from fire, explosion, or electrical fault.

items.title: going paperless
items.content: You may choose to receive most account, policy and servicing documents electronically instead of by post. When you go paperless, we will send notices to your registered email address and make documents available through your online account where applicable.

items.title: going paperless
items.content: Paperless delivery helps us reduce printing and postage, and it supports our wider commitments to efficiency and environmental responsibility. Some documents may still be sent in paper form where the law, regulation or the nature of the document requires it.

items.title: going paperless
items.content: To switch to paperless communications, you must keep a valid email address and access to your online account. It is your responsibility to tell us promptly if your email address changes or if you can no longer receive electronic documents.

items.title: going paperless
items.content: Where a document is issued electronically, it will be treated as delivered when we send the notification to your nominated email address or make it available in your secure online area, unless we tell you otherwise. You should check your inbox and spam or junk folders regularly.

items.title: going paperless
items.content: If you choose paperless service, we may not send duplicate paper copies unless you ask for one or we are required to do so. We may charge a reasonable fee for repeated paper copies where this is permitted and the request is not due to our error.

items.title: going paperless
items.content: We will use electronic communications only where we are satisfied that this is appropriate for the product or service in question. If at any time we are unable to deliver documents electronically, we may revert to paper delivery until the issue is resolved.

items.title: going paperless
items.content: You may withdraw your paperless preference at any time by contacting us through the channels we provide. Changes normally take effect within a reasonable period after we receive your instruction.

items.title: going paperless
items.content: Some important notices, including changes to terms, confirmations and regulatory information, may be sent by email or made available online. Please read these documents carefully, as they may affect your rights and obligations.

items.title: going paperless
items.content: If you share an email address or device with another person, you accept the risk that your communications may be seen by them. You should choose your paperless settings carefully and keep your login details secure.

items.title: going paperless
items.content: We may suspend paperless delivery if we suspect fraud, misuse or an account security issue, or if we need to protect you or the society. In those circumstances, we may send documents by post until normal service can resume.

items.title: going paperless
items.content: If you choose to go paperless, we will send your policy documents, statements and most customer communications by secure electronic means rather than by post. You must keep your email address and contact details up to date so that we can continue to serve you without delay.

items.title: going paperless
items.content: Paperless correspondence helps reduce paper use and supports quicker delivery of important information. Where electronic delivery is not available or is not suitable for a particular document, we may still write to you by post.

items.title: going paperless
items.content: You may change your preference to paperless communications at any time through your online account or by contacting us. Any change may take a short time to take effect, and some items already issued may still arrive by post.

items.title: going paperless
items.content: Where you have opted for paperless service, we will normally provide documents in a format that can be stored and printed by you. It is your responsibility to download and retain copies of any documents you may need later.

items.title: still wanting paper statements
items.content: If you still want paper statements, you may keep receiving them by post instead of by email or online message. This can be set on your account where available, subject to any other terms that apply to the product you hold.

items.title: still wanting paper statements
items.content: Paper statements are issued at the statement frequency that applies to your account or policy. Where a statement is available electronically, you may still choose to receive a printed copy.

items.title: still wanting paper statements
items.content: We may charge for additional paper copies of statements or documents where we are asked to reissue items already provided. Any such charge will be explained before it is applied.

items.title: still wanting paper statements
items.content: If you have asked for paper statements, please allow extra time for delivery by post. Postal delivery times may vary and are outside our control.

items.title: still wanting paper statements
items.content: You can change your preference for paper statements at any time by contacting us. Changes will normally take effect from the next available statement cycle.

items.title: still wanting paper statements
items.content: Where paper statements are sent, they will be posted to the last address we hold for you. It is your responsibility to let us know if your address changes.

items.title: still wanting paper statements
items.content: If you continue to receive paper statements, you remain responsible for checking them carefully and telling us promptly if anything is incorrect. This helps us resolve any issue without delay.

items.title: moving the direct debit date to payday
items.content: If you need your direct debit collected on or just after payday, you may request a change to your collection date. We will review the request against the payment schedule for your policy or account and confirm the earliest available date.

items.title: moving the direct debit date to payday
items.content: A direct debit date can usually be moved to suit your payday, provided the instruction remains within the collection window for that billing period. Any change will take effect from the next eligible collection, not retrospectively.

items.title: moving the direct debit date to payday
items.content: Where a customer’s payday falls later in the month, we may be able to align the direct debit collection accordingly. If the requested date is not available, we will offer the nearest suitable alternative.

items.title: moving the direct debit date to payday
items.content: To move a direct debit to payday, the account holder must ask us in advance of the next scheduled collection. We cannot guarantee a same-day amendment once the instruction has been submitted to the payer’s bank.

items.title: moving the direct debit date to payday
items.content: A change to the direct debit date does not alter the amount due, only the date on which it is collected. Any missed or returned payment will still need to be brought up to date in line with the terms of the agreement.

items.title: moving the direct debit date to payday
items.content: For monthly insurance premiums and savings collections, we will normally allow one direct debit date change each policy year at no charge. Additional amendments may be subject to administration rules set out in the product terms.

items.title: moving the direct debit date to payday
items.content: If moving the collection date to payday would create two payments too close together, we may advise a later change date to avoid duplicate collections. This is to ensure the instruction remains manageable and that no payment is taken in error.

items.title: moving the direct debit date to payday
items.content: Customers who are paid four-weekly or on a variable schedule should contact us before requesting a direct debit adjustment. We will use the most recent payroll date information available to set a collection date that is as close as practicable to payday.

items.title: moving the direct debit date to payday
items.content: Where a direct debit date is changed, the new date will appear on the next collection notice or account statement where applicable. Please keep your bank details and contact information up to date so we can confirm the amendment promptly.

items.title: moving the direct debit date to payday
items.content: If a customer is experiencing difficulty meeting a payment on the current date, moving the direct debit to payday may help prevent a missed collection. We will consider the request in a fair and consistent manner, subject to the product terms and any regulatory requirements.

items.title: moving the direct debit date to payday
items.content: If your salary date changes, you may ask us to move your direct debit to better match payday. We will usually be able to do this for your next collection, provided the request is made before the amendment cut-off date.

items.title: moving the direct debit date to payday
items.content: You can change your direct debit date once each month, subject to your payment plan and the rules of your bank. We may ask for confirmation that the new date is on or after your chosen payday.

items.title: moving the direct debit date to payday
items.content: Where a direct debit is set up for a mortgage or insurance premium, the date may be aligned to payday to help reduce missed payments. Any change will take effect from the next available collection cycle.

items.title: moving the direct debit date to payday
items.content: Requests to move a direct debit date should be made through online banking or by contacting our customer services team. If the new date falls on a non-working day, the collection will normally be taken on the next working day.

items.title: paying the premium annually for the discount
items.content: If you choose to pay your premium annually, we will apply the annual payment discount shown on your quote or renewal notice. The discount is only available where the full premium is paid in one instalment before the due date.

items.title: paying the premium annually for the discount
items.content: Annual payment may offer a lower overall cost than paying by instalments. Any discount is part of the premium calculation and is not separately refundable once cover has started, unless we agree otherwise under our cancellation terms.

items.title: paying the premium annually for the discount
items.content: Where an annual premium is selected, the full amount becomes due on the start date of the policy or on renewal, as applicable. If payment is not received when due, cover may be cancelled or may not begin.

items.title: paying the premium annually for the discount
items.content: The annual payment discount is subject to eligibility and may vary by product, risk and distribution channel. We may withdraw or amend the discount at any time for new business or renewal offers.

items.title: paying the premium annually for the discount
items.content: You may change from annual payment to instalments at renewal, subject to our agreement and any credit checks or charges that apply. Changing payment frequency may remove the annual discount and increase the total amount payable.

items.title: paying the premium annually for the discount
items.content: If you pay annually and then ask to cancel part-way through the policy term, any return premium will be calculated on the basis of the full premium paid. We may deduct any fees, charges or short-period adjustments permitted by the policy terms.

items.title: paying the premium annually for the discount
items.content: The annual payment discount is shown before tax, fees and any policy administration charges, unless stated otherwise. You should check your schedule to confirm the amount payable and the date by which payment must be received.

items.title: preferring email to phone calls
items.content: Where possible, members should use email rather than telephoning us, as this gives us a written record of the request and helps us respond more efficiently. Email is especially useful for non-urgent enquiries, document submissions and status updates.

items.title: preferring email to phone calls
items.content: For routine servicing of accounts and policies, email is our preferred contact method. It enables us to route your message to the correct team and reduces delays caused by call waiting times.

items.title: preferring email to phone calls
items.content: If you have supporting documents to send, please use email rather than a phone call. This allows us to receive and review the information in full without the need for a repeat contact.

items.title: preferring email to phone calls
items.content: We encourage members to contact us by email in the first instance for all matters that do not require immediate action. Telephone lines are reserved primarily for urgent issues and time-sensitive claims matters.

items.title: preferring email to phone calls
items.content: Using email helps us maintain an accurate record of instructions, disclosures and follow-up actions. This supports consistency in our service and reduces the risk of misunderstanding.

items.title: preferring email to phone calls
items.content: When a matter can be handled by either telephone or email, staff should direct members to email unless the circumstances justify a call. This applies in particular to general enquiries, address changes and requests for copies of documents.

items.title: preferring email to phone calls
items.content: We prefer email for most written correspondence because it allows members to set out their query clearly and attach any relevant evidence. It also enables us to respond in a structured manner and keep the conversation in one place.

items.title: preferring email to phone calls
items.content: Members should be advised that email is the quickest method for submitting non-urgent requests outside our busiest call periods. Where a phone call is not necessary, email helps us deal with enquiries in order of receipt.

items.title: preferring email to phone calls
items.content: Our service standard is to use email as the default channel for routine communication unless the member asks otherwise or the situation requires immediate discussion. This approach supports efficient handling across our savings, mortgage and insurance teams.

items.title: preferring email to phone calls
items.content: Please use email rather than phoning us where you need to provide detail, confirmation or documentation. A written message gives us a clear audit trail and helps ensure your request is actioned correctly.

items.title: preferring email to phone calls
items.content: Where possible, please use email rather than telephoning us. Email provides a written record of your query and helps us route your request to the correct team more quickly.

items.title: preferring email to phone calls
items.content: Our preferred method of contact for non-urgent matters is email. This allows us to review your information properly and respond in a clear and traceable way.

items.title: preferring email to phone calls
items.content: If you need to send supporting documents, email is usually the best option. It enables us to receive attachments securely and link them directly to your case.

items.title: preferring email to phone calls
items.content: We may ask members to confirm routine changes by email rather than by phone. This is to reduce errors and ensure there is a record of the instruction given.

items.title: calls only after work hours
items.content: We will only make outbound calls to members after normal working hours where there is a clear operational need and the contact is permitted by the member's recorded preferences. Such calls must be made courteously and kept as brief as possible.

items.title: calls only after work hours
items.content: Calls after work hours must not be placed unless the matter cannot reasonably wait until the next business day. Staff must first consider whether a secure message, email or written letter would be more appropriate.

items.title: calls only after work hours
items.content: When a member has asked not to be contacted by telephone outside working hours, that instruction must be respected. Any exception requires authorisation in line with the relevant team procedure.

items.title: calls only after work hours
items.content: If an after-hours call is necessary, the caller must state the society's name promptly and explain why the contact is taking place at that time. The member's convenience and privacy must be taken into account throughout the call.

items.title: calls only after work hours
items.content: After-hours calls must not be used for sales, retention or any activity that could reasonably be delayed until the next working day. They are reserved for urgent servicing, claim handling or security-related matters only.

items.title: calls only after work hours
items.content: Before calling after work hours, staff must check the member's preferred contact times and any vulnerability notes recorded on the account. Where there is any doubt, the call must be deferred.

items.title: calls only after work hours
items.content: Members contacted after work hours should be given the option to continue, arrange a call-back, or request that the matter be handled in writing. Their preference must be recorded on the system without delay.

items.title: no marketing please
items.content: If a claim is settled on a cash basis, we will pay a fair amount to reflect the cost of repair, replacement or reinstatement, less any deductions stated in the policy. We may ask for evidence of ownership, age, condition or value before making payment. Where appropriate, we may appoint suppliers or loss adjusters to assess the claim.

items.title: no marketing please
items.content: You must take reasonable steps to prevent further damage after an insured event. This includes making the property safe, protecting it from the weather and arranging temporary repairs where necessary. We will expect any emergency costs to be reasonable and supported by receipts where available.

items.title: no marketing please
items.content: Escape of water claims should be reported to us as soon as reasonably possible. We may require the affected system or appliance to be isolated, drained down or repaired before further loss occurs. Damage caused by gradual leakage, wear and tear or lack of maintenance is not covered.

items.title: no marketing please
items.content: Storm damage is considered against the usual weather conditions for the area and the condition of the property at the time of loss. We do not treat every period of heavy rain or wind as a storm for insurance purposes. We will look at whether the event was exceptional and whether the damage was directly caused by it.

items.title: no marketing please
items.content: For theft claims, there must be evidence of forced and violent entry unless the policy states otherwise. We may ask for a police crime reference number and a full list of missing items. Keys, cards and similar access devices must be safeguarded at all times.

items.title: no marketing please
items.content: Subsidence is a gradual movement of the ground beneath a building and may be evidenced by cracks, sloping floors or sticking doors and windows. Where subsidence is suspected, we may request site investigations before confirming cover or settlement. Damage caused by settlement, heave or landslip is handled in accordance with the subsidence section of the policy.

items.title: no marketing please
items.content: Flood cover applies to damage caused by the escaping or overflowing of water from rivers, streams, the sea, drainage systems or surface water following heavy rainfall. We will consider the likely source of the water, the extent of any ingress and the measures taken to reduce the damage. Pre-existing damp, wear and tear or poor maintenance are not flood damage.

items.title: no marketing please
items.content: When a claim is accepted, we may arrange a repair through one of our approved contractors. If you choose not to use our repair network, any cash settlement will usually be limited to what it would have cost us to repair the damage. Any upgrade or betterment is your responsibility unless the policy provides otherwise.

items.title: no marketing please
items.content: You must tell us about any material change in risk as soon as you are aware of it. This includes leaving the property unoccupied for an extended period, starting building work or using the home for a business purpose. Failure to disclose a material change may affect cover or the outcome of a claim.

items.title: no marketing please
items.content: Where a claim is disputed, you may ask us to review the decision through our complaints process. If you remain dissatisfied after we have issued our final response, you may refer the matter to the Financial Ombudsman Service within the relevant time limits. We will provide details of this right in our final response letter.

items.title: no marketing please
items.content: If you discover water leaking from a pipe, appliance or roof, you must take reasonable steps to prevent further damage. Where it is safe to do so, stop the source, isolate the supply, and arrange suitable temporary repairs without delay. You should also tell us as soon as reasonably practicable.

items.title: no marketing please
items.content: For storm damage, we expect customers to make the property safe if possible and to keep any damaged parts available for inspection. Temporary boarding, tarpaulins or similar protective measures may be arranged where needed to reduce further loss. We may ask for photographs and details of the weather conditions at the time of the incident.

items.title: no marketing please
items.content: Our subsidence cover does not apply to gradual settlement, shrinkage or expansion which is not caused by subsidence. We may require a period of monitoring and further investigation before agreeing a claim. Any repairs should not be started until we have had a reasonable opportunity to inspect, unless immediate action is needed to protect the property.

items.title: no marketing please
items.content: In the event of a theft, you must report the matter to the police promptly and obtain a crime reference number where available. You should also tell us what has been taken, when the loss was discovered, and whether there were signs of forced entry. We may ask for proof of ownership or purchase where this is reasonably necessary to assess the claim.

items.title: how the member dividend is paid
items.content: The member dividend is declared by the Board when the Society has made a surplus and retained sufficient capital to meet regulatory requirements. It is not guaranteed and may vary from year to year.

items.title: how the member dividend is paid
items.content: Where a dividend is declared, it is ordinarily paid to eligible members by bank transfer to the current account or nominated account held on the Society’s records. Members should ensure their payment details are kept up to date.

items.title: how the member dividend is paid
items.content: Eligibility for the member dividend is assessed by reference to the qualifying criteria set by the Society for the relevant year. These criteria may include active membership and the holding of eligible products for the required period.

items.title: how the member dividend is paid
items.content: The Board may determine the amount of the dividend, the payment method and the payment date at its discretion. Any decision will be made in accordance with the Society’s constitution and applicable law.

items.title: how the member dividend is paid
items.content: If a member has an outstanding arrears balance, unpaid fee or other debit on an eligible account, the Society may apply the dividend to reduce that balance before any residual sum is paid. This is done in line with the terms governing the account.

items.title: how the member dividend is paid
items.content: Dividend payments are made after the annual accounts have been approved and the relevant declaration has been authorised. The Society will notify members when a payment has been arranged.

items.title: how the member dividend is paid
items.content: Where the Society is unable to make a dividend payment to the nominated account, the amount may be held pending receipt of correct payment instructions. The Society may require proof of identity or account ownership before release.

items.title: how the member dividend is paid
items.content: The member dividend is treated as a distribution of surplus and is separate from interest, premium refunds or claim payments. It does not form part of any insured loss settlement or product guarantee.

items.title: how the member dividend is paid
items.content: Members who are entitled to a dividend will usually receive a single payment for the relevant year, unless the Board resolves otherwise. Partial or interim dividend payments are only made where expressly announced by the Society.

items.title: how the member dividend is paid
items.content: Any dividend paid in error may be recovered by the Society, including by set-off against future payments or account credits where permitted. The Society may correct administrative errors without prejudice to its right to seek repayment.

items.title: how the member dividend is paid
items.content: The member dividend, when declared by the Board, is paid only to eligible members in accordance with the Society’s rules and the terms set out for the relevant dividend year. Payment may be made by bank transfer, cheque or such other method as the Society may reasonably specify.

items.title: how the member dividend is paid
items.content: Where a member holds more than one qualifying account or policy, the dividend is assessed on the basis of the eligibility criteria applicable to each product and will not be paid more than once in respect of the same qualifying holding. The Society may aggregate qualifying balances or premiums for the purpose of determining entitlement.

items.title: how the member dividend is paid
items.content: The dividend is discretionary and is not guaranteed. A decision to declare or vary the amount of any dividend rests entirely with the Board, having regard to the Society’s financial position, regulatory requirements and the interests of members as a whole.

items.title: how the member dividend is paid
items.content: Any dividend payment will normally be made after the annual results have been approved and the eligibility records have been checked. If a member’s details are incomplete or out of date, payment may be delayed until the Society is satisfied that the correct recipient has been identified.

items.title: reinvesting the dividend into savings
items.content: Members may choose to reinvest any dividend credited to their account into an eligible Larkmere savings account. Where this option is selected, the dividend is applied in accordance with the account terms then in force. The reinvested amount will form part of the cleared balance of the receiving account.

items.title: reinvesting the dividend into savings
items.content: A dividend may be paid into savings only where the member holds a qualifying account capable of receiving the credit. If no eligible savings account is held, the dividend will be handled under the society’s standard dividend payment arrangements. Any balance created by reinvestment remains subject to the relevant product conditions.

items.title: reinvesting the dividend into savings
items.content: Reinvesting the dividend allows members to leave their surplus with the society rather than withdrawing it. The amount credited will retain its character as dividend for tax and reporting purposes, where applicable. Interest, if any, will then be calculated in the normal way under the savings account terms.

items.title: reinvesting the dividend into savings
items.content: Where a member has instructed Larkmere Mutual to reinvest dividend into savings, the society will act on that instruction for future distributions until it is amended or withdrawn. Instructions must be clear and current at the time the dividend is processed. The society may refuse to apply an instruction that cannot be matched to an eligible account.

items.title: reinvesting the dividend into savings
items.content: Dividend reinvestment is intended to support members who wish to build their savings over time. The credited sum may be subject to minimum or maximum limits set out in the relevant savings product summary. Members should review those limits before selecting reinvestment.

items.title: reinvesting the dividend into savings
items.content: If a dividend is reinvested, the credit will usually appear on the savings account statement as a dividend entry. This entry will show the date of application and the amount credited. No separate withdrawal is required where reinvestment has been selected in advance.

items.title: reinvesting the dividend into savings
items.content: The society will not combine dividend reinvestment with any savings account that is closed, frozen or otherwise unable to accept credits. In such cases, the dividend will be held only for as long as permitted by the society’s procedures. Members may be contacted to provide an alternative receiving account.

items.title: roof tiles blown off in a storm
items.content: If storm conditions have lifted and roof tiles have been blown off, you should make the area safe as soon as it is practicable to do so. Do not put yourself at risk by climbing onto a damaged roof or handling loose tiles that may fall.

items.title: roof tiles blown off in a storm
items.content: Where roof tiles have been displaced by storm, we will normally ask you to take reasonable emergency steps to prevent further damage. This may include covering exposed areas temporarily and arranging for urgent attendance by a qualified contractor.

items.title: roof tiles blown off in a storm
items.content: Storm damage to roof tiles is considered under the buildings section of the policy, subject to the terms, exclusions and excess that apply. We will assess the claim against the weather conditions and the condition of the roof at the time of loss.

items.title: roof tiles blown off in a storm
items.content: You must tell us about roof tiles blown off in a storm as soon as reasonably possible after the event. Early notification helps us to record the cause of loss and advise you on any immediate protective action.

items.title: roof tiles blown off in a storm
items.content: If wind has lifted or removed roof tiles, we may request photographs of the damage and any debris on the ground. Where safe to do so, please retain any broken tiles that may assist with our assessment or repairs.

items.title: roof tiles blown off in a storm
items.content: We do not expect members to carry out permanent repairs before we have had a reasonable opportunity to inspect the damage, unless urgent safety reasons require immediate action. Temporary repairs should be limited to preventing further damage only.

items.title: roof tiles blown off in a storm
items.content: Damage limited to a few loose or broken tiles may be settled by arranging repair rather than full roof replacement, depending on the extent of the loss. Where matching materials are no longer available, we will consider the nearest suitable equivalent in accordance with the policy wording.

items.title: roof tiles blown off in a storm
items.content: If the roof was already in poor repair, or if tiles were loose, missing or deteriorated before the storm, we may reduce or decline the claim for the affected part of the damage. The policy does not cover wear and tear, gradual deterioration or lack of maintenance.

items.title: roof tiles blown off in a storm
items.content: We may appoint a surveyor or loss adjuster where the cause of damage, the age of the roof or the extent of tile loss needs further checking. Their report will help us decide whether the damage was caused by storm and what repairs are reasonable.

items.title: roof tiles blown off in a storm
items.content: Where roof tiles are blown off and water enters the home, any resulting internal damage may also be considered as part of the same claim, subject to the policy terms. You should take prompt steps to minimise further water ingress once it is safe to do so.

items.title: roof tiles blown off in a storm
items.content: If storm winds have blown roof tiles from your home, you must take reasonable steps to prevent further damage as soon as it is safe to do so. This may include placing a temporary cover over the exposed area and arranging an urgent repair. You should keep any invoices and photographs for your claim.

items.title: roof tiles blown off in a storm
items.content: We will usually treat blown-off roof tiles as storm damage where the weather conditions were sufficiently severe and the loss was sudden and accidental. Wear and tear, lack of maintenance, or existing damage is not covered under this section. The condition of the roof before the event may affect our decision.

items.title: roof tiles blown off in a storm
items.content: If roof tiles are missing after a storm, please tell us promptly and do not wait for the next inspection or repair visit. Delay may allow rainwater to enter the property and could increase the damage. We may ask you to confirm whether any internal ceilings, walls or contents have been affected.

items.title: roof tiles blown off in a storm
items.content: Where it is safe, please take clear photographs of the roof damage from ground level and of any broken tiles on the ground. Do not attempt to climb onto the roof unless you are competent and it is safe to do so. We may use the photographs to assess whether a temporary repair is needed.

items.title: roof tiles blown off in a storm
items.content: Our settlement may include the cost of replacing the damaged tiles on a like-for-like basis, subject to the terms of your policy. If matching tiles are no longer available, we will consider the closest suitable alternative. Any improvement beyond the original condition is not insured.

items.title: roof tiles blown off in a storm
items.content: Storm damage to roof tiles is assessed against the weather event and the condition of the property. If the roof had loose, cracked or slipped tiles beforehand, we may reduce or decline the claim for that part of the loss. This is because we do not insure gradual deterioration.

items.title: roof tiles blown off in a storm
items.content: You should make every effort to limit further water ingress after tiles are blown off, but only if you can do so safely. If you need emergency boarding or tarpaulin work, keep the contractor's details and the date of the work. Reasonable emergency repairs are normally considered as part of the claim.

items.title: roof tiles blown off in a storm
items.content: If the storm has affected a shared or adjoining roof, you must tell us whether the damage relates to your own insured section. We may also ask for details from any managing agent, landlord or neighbour where responsibility is unclear. We can only pay for the portion of damage that is covered under your policy.

items.title: roof tiles blown off in a storm
items.content: Where roof tiles have blown off and there is no visible internal damage, we may still require a survey before agreeing permanent repairs. This helps us confirm the extent of the loss and whether the roof needs partial or full replacement. You should not arrange extensive work until we have had a reasonable opportunity to inspect or authorise it, unless urgent action is required.

items.title: roof tiles blown off in a storm
items.content: Claims for storm damage to roof tiles may be declined if the weather at the insured location did not amount to a storm under the policy definition. We may refer to records from the Met Office and other sources when considering wind speed and local conditions. A strong wind alone is not always sufficient for cover.

items.title: roof tiles blown off in a storm
items.content: If roof tiles are blown off by a storm, we will assess the damage against the storm terms in your policy. We may ask for evidence that the weather conditions at the time were severe enough to meet our definition of storm. Temporary repairs should be arranged promptly to prevent further damage to the home.

items.title: roof tiles blown off in a storm
items.content: Storm damage to roof tiles is covered when the loss has been caused directly by high winds and not by wear and tear, poor maintenance or gradual deterioration. Missing, loose or cracked tiles that were already in poor condition may not be insured. We may reduce or decline a claim where pre-existing defects have contributed to the loss.

items.title: roof tiles blown off in a storm
items.content: Where roof tiles are blown off, you must take reasonable steps to protect the property from further damage. This may include covering exposed areas and arranging emergency repairs. Please keep receipts for any reasonable expenses incurred in making the property safe.

items.title: roof tiles blown off in a storm
items.content: Our claims team may request photographs of the roof, details of the date and time of the storm, and any local weather reports. This information helps us confirm the cause of the damage and determine whether the event falls within the policy cover. We may also inspect the roof before authorising full repairs.

items.title: roof tiles blown off in a storm
items.content: We do not pay for damage to roof tiles caused by lack of maintenance, defective workmanship or gradual erosion. However, where a storm has lifted and scattered otherwise sound tiles, we will consider the resulting damage under the buildings section of the policy. The settlement will be based on the reasonable cost of repair or replacement using matching materials where available.

items.title: roof tiles blown off in a storm
items.content: If a storm has removed roof tiles and made the home unsafe, you should contact us as soon as reasonably practicable. We may arrange emergency assistance or approve a contractor to carry out temporary work. Any permanent repair must be agreed with us before it is completed, unless this is impossible in an emergency.

items.title: roof tiles blown off in a storm
items.content: The policy covers sudden and unforeseen damage caused by storm, including the loss of roof tiles, where the storm is the effective cause of the damage. It does not cover cosmetic blemishes, pre-existing damage, or any repair needed solely because the roof was near the end of its serviceable life. We will consider each claim on its facts and the evidence provided.

items.title: roof tiles blown off in a storm
items.content: Where roof tiles have been blown off, you should make sure the loft and rooms below are protected from rainwater ingress. If water enters the property as a result of the storm damage, we will consider the resulting internal damage under the relevant section of cover. Failure to take reasonable precautions may affect the amount we pay.

items.title: roof tiles blown off in a storm
items.content: Any claim for storm damage to roof tiles must be reported as soon as possible after the event. Delay may make it harder for us to verify the cause and extent of the loss. We may refuse part of a claim where preventable further damage has occurred because repairs were not arranged promptly.

items.title: roof tiles blown off in a storm
items.content: If we accept a storm claim for blown roof tiles, we will normally pay for tiles of a similar type, quality and appearance where available. Where exact matching is not possible, we will only pay what is reasonable for the repair. We will not improve the roof beyond its pre-loss condition.

items.title: roof tiles blown off in a storm
items.content: If wind in a storm has blown roof tiles from your home, you should make the area safe as soon as possible and report the damage to us without delay. We may ask you to arrange a temporary repair to prevent further water ingress while we assess the claim.

items.title: roof tiles blown off in a storm
items.content: Storm damage to roof tiles is covered where the weather event meets our definition of storm and the loss was not caused by wear and tear, gradual deterioration or poor maintenance. We will not pay for pre-existing defects that would have allowed the tiles to lift or fail in ordinary weather.

items.title: roof tiles blown off in a storm
items.content: You must take reasonable steps to protect the property after roof tiles have been blown off, including covering exposed areas if it can be done safely. Any emergency work should be limited to what is necessary to reduce the risk of further damage.

items.title: roof tiles blown off in a storm
items.content: Where roof tiles are lost in a storm, our settlement will usually be based on the cost of replacing the damaged tiles with matching or suitable equivalent tiles where available. If exact matching materials are no longer obtainable, we may contribute towards a reasonable alternative repair.

items.title: roof tiles blown off in a storm
items.content: We may appoint a surveyor or loss adjuster to inspect the roof before permanent repairs are carried out. Please keep any damaged tiles, photographs and receipts for emergency repairs, as these may be needed to support your claim.

items.title: a fence blown down
items.content: If a fence is blown down in a storm, we will consider whether the damage was caused by an insured event under your buildings or home insurance. Damage that is solely due to wear, decay, lack of maintenance or gradual deterioration is not covered.

items.title: a fence blown down
items.content: You should make the area safe as soon as possible after the loss. Where a fence has become unstable or fallen into a public area, arrange temporary securing or warning measures without delay.

items.title: a fence blown down
items.content: Please retain any damaged sections, photographs and any receipts for emergency repairs. We may ask for these to help us assess the cause and extent of the damage.

items.title: a fence blown down
items.content: Where fencing forms part of the insured buildings, we will normally look to repair or replace it on a like-for-like basis, subject to the terms, limits and excess of your policy. We do not provide betterment for pre-existing deterioration.

items.title: a fence blown down
items.content: If the fence was blown down by high winds, we may ask for evidence that the weather conditions were sufficiently severe in the relevant area. We may use publicly available weather information, including from the Met Office, when considering the claim.

items.title: a fence blown down
items.content: We do not cover damage caused by faulty workmanship, defective materials or an existing structural weakness. If these factors contributed to the fence failing, settlement may be reduced or declined.

items.title: a fence blown down
items.content: Temporary repairs are intended to prevent further damage and protect the property from unauthorised access. We may reimburse reasonable emergency costs where they are necessary and directly related to the insured loss.

items.title: a fence blown down
items.content: Where the fence borders a shared boundary, responsibility for repair may depend on ownership and any agreement in place. You should provide any available evidence showing whether the fence belongs to you, a neighbour or is jointly maintained.

items.title: a fence blown down
items.content: If a fence collapse has caused damage to neighbouring property, you must notify us promptly. Your liability cover may respond if you are legally responsible for the damage and the incident is covered by your policy.

items.title: a fence blown down
items.content: Claims for fences are assessed in the same way as other storm damage, with attention to the cause, the condition of the item before the storm and the scope of the loss. Our decision will be based on the policy wording and the facts of the claim.

items.title: a fence blown down
items.content: If a fence is blown down in a storm, we will consider whether the damage was caused by an insured event and whether the fence formed part of the insured property. You must take reasonable steps to prevent any further damage and keep any damaged sections safe until we have had the chance to assess the claim.

items.title: a fence blown down
items.content: Where a fence has been damaged by high winds, we may ask for photographs showing the condition before and after the event, together with details of any storm warnings issued by the Met Office. We may also request evidence of the fence type, age and maintenance history.

items.title: a fence blown down
items.content: A fence that has simply deteriorated through wear and tear, age or lack of maintenance is not covered. If a storm has exposed a pre-existing weakness, we may reduce or decline the settlement to reflect that condition.

items.title: a fence blown down
items.content: If the whole fence panel has been blown over but the posts remain sound, we will normally look to repair or replace only the damaged section. We do not automatically replace adjoining undamaged sections unless they are no longer suitable to match or support the repaired area.

items.title: a fence blown down
items.content: You should make any temporary repairs that are necessary to secure the boundary and prevent injury, but only where it is safe to do so. Reasonable emergency costs may be covered if they are necessary to protect the property from further loss.

items.title: a fence blown down
items.content: We will not usually pay for damage to a fence caused by gradual movement, defective construction or rot. Where wind damage occurs together with one of these conditions, we will assess the extent to which each cause contributed to the loss.

items.title: a fence blown down
items.content: If your fence was blown down and has caused damage to a neighbour’s property, you must tell us at once. Cover for liability may apply only if the claim arises from a risk insured under your policy and falls within the policy terms.

items.title: a fence blown down
items.content: Replacement fencing will normally be calculated on a like-for-like basis, allowing for similar materials and standard dimensions. We do not provide an automatic upgrade to a more expensive or decorative specification unless this is required for repair consistency.

items.title: a fence blown down
items.content: Following a storm, loose fence panels, nails and broken timber should be removed where safe and practicable. You must not dispose of damaged parts until we have confirmed whether an inspection or salvage is required.

items.title: a fence blown down
items.content: Where a fence is shared with another property, responsibility for repair may depend on ownership, boundary arrangement and the cause of damage. We may ask for deeds, title information or other documents before confirming whether the loss is covered.

items.title: a fence blown down
items.content: If a fence is blown down by storm, you should take reasonable steps to prevent further damage to the insured property. Where it is safe to do so, secure loose panels, remove hazardous debris and make temporary repairs until a permanent repair can be arranged.

items.title: a fence blown down
items.content: We may ask for evidence of the damage, including clear photographs before any repairs are carried out. Please keep receipts for any emergency work or materials, as these may be considered as part of your claim.

items.title: a fence blown down
items.content: Damage to fences is covered only where the cause is an insured event and the damage is sudden and accidental. Wear and tear, lack of maintenance and gradual deterioration are not insured.

items.title: a fence blown down
items.content: A fence section blown over by high winds will usually be assessed as part of the buildings claim if it forms part of the property boundary. We will consider whether the fence was in a reasonable state of repair before the event.

items.title: a fence blown down
items.content: We do not expect you to make permanent repairs before we have had an opportunity to inspect the damage, unless immediate action is needed to make the property safe. Any temporary measures should be proportionate to the loss.

items.title: a fence blown down
items.content: If a fallen fence has caused injury or obstructed a public pavement, you must report the matter promptly to the relevant authority where necessary. You remain responsible for keeping the property safe and not creating a hazard.

items.title: a fence blown down
items.content: Claims for storm damage to fences may be reduced where the fence was already weakened, rotten or poorly maintained. We will not pay for damage that would have happened in any case because of the fence's condition.

items.title: a fence blown down
items.content: Where a fence is shared with a neighbouring property, we may need confirmation of ownership and responsibility before settling the claim. We may also ask whether the neighbouring owner has made, or intends to make, a separate claim.

items.title: a damaged shed or outbuilding
items.content: If a shed, garage or other outbuilding is damaged by an insured event, we will assess the damage in line with your buildings cover, provided it forms part of the premises insured and is not excluded. We may ask for photographs, receipts or other evidence to confirm the age, construction and condition of the structure. Any repair or replacement will be based on the terms and limits of your policy.

items.title: a damaged shed or outbuilding
items.content: Damage to a detached outbuilding caused by storm will only be covered where the building is soundly constructed and properly maintained. We do not pay for wear and tear, rot, gradual deterioration or damage arising from defective workmanship or poor maintenance. Where the structure has not been kept in reasonable repair, we may reduce or decline a claim.

items.title: a damaged shed or outbuilding
items.content: Contents kept in a shed or outbuilding are only covered if your policy includes the relevant contents cover and the item is not subject to any special limit or exclusion. High-value items may be subject to a lower limit when stored away from the main home. You should check your schedule for any restrictions applying to garden equipment, bicycles or tools.

items.title: a damaged shed or outbuilding
items.content: Where a shed roof has been lifted or broken by wind, we will consider whether the event was storm as defined by the policy. Rainwater entering through an opening made by insured damage may be included, but damage caused by pre-existing weakness or poor repair is not covered. We may appoint a loss adjuster if the cause or extent of damage is unclear.

items.title: a damaged shed or outbuilding
items.content: We do not cover damage to fences, gates or detached outbuildings caused by gradual weathering alone. If an outbuilding is damaged by impact, fire, escape of water or another insured peril, the claim will be considered under the relevant section of cover. Any resulting loss must be directly linked to the insured event.

items.title: a damaged shed or outbuilding
items.content: If a shed or summerhouse is used for business purposes, additional conditions may apply. Cover may be restricted or excluded where the building is used to store stock, tools or equipment for a trade. You must tell us if the use of an outbuilding changes in a way that affects the risk.

items.title: a damaged shed or outbuilding
items.content: We will not pay for the full cost of replacing a damaged outbuilding unless repair is not reasonably possible. Where a repair is practical, we may settle on that basis rather than authorising complete replacement. Any settlement will take account of materials of similar quality and the reasonable cost of labour.

items.title: a damaged shed or outbuilding
items.content: Break-in damage to a shed or outbuilding may be covered where there is evidence of forcible and violent entry. We may require confirmation that the premises were secured and that any locks, hasps or doors were properly fitted at the time of the incident.
