Theft claims should be reported to the police without delay.

items.title: a damaged shed or outbuilding
items.content: If an outbuilding is unsafe following an insured incident, you must take reasonable steps to prevent further damage or injury. This may include boarding up openings, removing water where safe to do so, or arranging temporary protection. We may not cover avoidable additional loss if reasonable precautions are not taken.

items.title: a damaged shed or outbuilding
items.content: We will not cover damage to a shed caused by subsidence unless subsidence is specifically included under your buildings cover and the policy terms are met. Subsidence claims are subject to a separate assessment process and may require specialist reports. Damage due to settlement, shrinkage or movement not meeting the policy definition is excluded.

items.title: a damaged shed or outbuilding
items.content: A shed, garage or other domestic outbuilding is covered only where it forms part of the insured property and is used for domestic purposes. Damage caused by storm, fire, theft or vandalism may be covered, subject to the policy terms and limits shown in the schedule.

items.title: a damaged shed or outbuilding
items.content: You must take reasonable steps to prevent further damage to a damaged outbuilding and to protect any contents that remain inside. Temporary repairs may be made immediately, provided they are necessary and can be evidenced with photographs or other records.

items.title: a damaged shed or outbuilding
items.content: We do not cover wear and tear, gradual deterioration, rot, rust or faulty maintenance affecting a shed or outbuilding. Damage that arises because the structure was already in poor repair may be excluded in whole or in part.

items.title: a damaged shed or outbuilding
items.content: If a shed or outbuilding has been damaged by escape of water, you should isolate the source where safe to do so and arrange prompt drying of the affected area. We may ask for proof that the building was properly maintained and protected against freezing conditions.

items.title: a damaged shed or outbuilding
items.content: Where theft from a shed or outbuilding is claimed, there must be clear evidence of forcible and violent entry or exit unless the policy wording states otherwise. Contents left unsecured may not be covered, and special limits may apply to bicycles, tools and gardening equipment.

items.title: a damaged shed or outbuilding
items.content: Storm damage to a shed or outbuilding will normally be considered only where the event meets our definition of storm. We may inspect weather conditions, the condition of the structure and whether damage to nearby properties is consistent with the claimed cause.

items.title: a damaged shed or outbuilding
items.content: We may repair, replace or settle the claim in cash at our option, depending on the extent of the damage. Where the outbuilding can be economically repaired, we will not normally pay to replace it in full unless the damage cannot be reasonably rectified.

items.title: a damaged shed or outbuilding
items.content: Any outbuilding used for business purposes, renting, storage for reward or as a separate dwelling is not covered unless specifically noted on the policy schedule. You must tell us if the use of the building changes during the period of insurance.

items.title: a damaged shed or outbuilding
items.content: If a damaged shed contains items that are insured separately elsewhere in the policy, those items may be assessed under the relevant section rather than the buildings section. The total amount payable will not exceed the applicable limit for each part of the claim.

items.title: a damaged shed or outbuilding
items.content: After a claim involving a damaged outbuilding, we may require you to provide proof of ownership, photographs of the undamaged condition and estimates for repair from suitable tradespeople. Failure to cooperate fully may delay settlement or affect the amount paid.

items.title: a damaged shed or outbuilding
items.content: We cover damage to a shed or other outbuilding only where it forms part of the insured home and is used for domestic purposes. The building must be maintained in a reasonable state of repair and construction. Contents stored in the outbuilding are covered only if your policy schedule says so.

items.title: a burst pipe in winter
items.content: Where freezing temperatures are forecast, you must take reasonable steps to protect your home from escape of water. This includes keeping the heating on low, insulating exposed pipes and ensuring the property is checked regularly if left unoccupied.

items.title: a burst pipe in winter
items.content: If a pipe bursts, turn off the water at the stopcock without delay and, where safe to do so, switch off the relevant electricity supply in affected areas. You should then take immediate action to limit further damage and arrange temporary drying or repairs.

items.title: a burst pipe in winter
items.content: Claims arising from burst pipes in winter are considered under the escape of water section of the home policy. Cover applies subject to the terms, conditions, limits and exclusions shown in the schedule and wording.

items.title: a burst pipe in winter
items.content: We expect members to maintain their homes in a good state of repair and to act promptly when signs of frost risk or leakage appear. Failure to take reasonable precautions may affect the outcome of a claim.

items.title: a burst pipe in winter
items.content: If the property is likely to be unoccupied during cold weather, the heating should be left set to a minimum background temperature, usually no lower than 12°C, unless otherwise agreed with us. Draining down water systems may also be required in some circumstances.

items.title: a burst pipe in winter
items.content: Damage caused by gradual seepage, poor maintenance or pre-existing defects is not the same as sudden bursting of a pipe and may not be covered. We may ask for evidence that the plumbing system had been maintained appropriately.

items.title: a burst pipe in winter
items.content: You must notify us as soon as reasonably possible after a burst pipe has occurred. Early reporting helps us control the loss, arrange emergency repairs where appropriate and assess any resulting damage.

items.title: a burst pipe in winter
items.content: We may require photographs, repair invoices and details of any steps taken to prevent recurrence. Where a contractor is instructed, only reasonable and necessary costs will be considered for settlement.

items.title: a burst pipe in winter
items.content: If the burst pipe has affected flooring, walls or fixtures, we will assess the damage to those parts of the building or contents that have been directly damaged by the escape of water. We will not pay to improve the property beyond its original condition.

items.title: a burst pipe in winter
items.content: Members are advised to know the location of the main stopcock and any local isolating valves before winter sets in. In an emergency, quick isolation of the water supply can materially reduce the extent of loss.

items.title: a burst pipe in winter
items.content: If a pipe bursts during cold weather, you should take immediate steps to stop the flow of water and protect the home from further damage. Turn off the main water supply if it is safe to do so and arrange for urgent repairs by a qualified tradesperson.

items.title: a burst pipe in winter
items.content: Where a burst pipe has caused water damage, you must tell us as soon as reasonably possible. Please keep damaged items, photographs and any repair invoices, as these may be required when we assess the claim.

items.title: a burst pipe in winter
items.content: We expect you to keep your home heated appropriately in winter to help reduce the risk of pipes freezing and bursting. If a property is left unattended, reasonable precautions should be taken to prevent frost damage.

items.title: a burst pipe in winter
items.content: Our cover does not extend to damage caused by a gradual leak or by a lack of maintenance. A burst pipe may be covered where the escape of water is sudden and accidental, subject to the terms, limits and exclusions of the policy.

items.title: a burst pipe in winter
items.content: If water is escaping from a burst pipe, please move belongings away from the affected area where it is safe to do so. You should also make any necessary temporary arrangements to reduce further loss, including isolating electrics if water is near sockets or appliances.

items.title: a burst pipe in winter
items.content: When a claim relates to freezing conditions, we may ask what steps were taken to protect the property before the pipe burst. This may include evidence of heating, insulation, lagging or regular visits to an unoccupied home.

items.title: a burst pipe in winter
items.content: Repairs to the pipe itself are not usually covered under the buildings section where the damage is due to wear and tear, corrosion or poor workmanship. We will consider the resulting insured damage to the home in line with the policy wording.

items.title: a burst pipe in winter
items.content: If a burst pipe has made the home temporarily uninhabitable, we will review whether alternative accommodation is covered under the policy. Any assistance will depend on the circumstances of the loss and the extent of the damage.

items.title: a burst pipe in winter
items.content: You should not discard any damaged fittings or materials without first checking whether they need to be inspected. In some cases, we may appoint a loss adjuster or request further evidence before confirming settlement.

items.title: a burst pipe in winter
items.content: To help prevent winter claims, you should drain down outside taps and protect exposed pipework before periods of severe frost. Where reasonable precautions have not been taken, this may affect the outcome of a claim.

items.title: a burst pipe in winter
items.content: If a pipe bursts in freezing weather, you must take immediate steps to stop further leakage and damage. Turn off the water supply at the stopcock where it is safe to do so, and arrange for a competent tradesperson to make the necessary repairs as soon as possible.

items.title: a burst pipe in winter
items.content: You should drain down the system if there is a risk of further freezing, provided this can be done safely. Larkmere Mutual expects you to act promptly to protect the home from avoidable loss.

items.title: a burst pipe in winter
items.content: Where water has escaped from a burst pipe, you must dry the affected area and ventilate the property without delay. Any soaked carpets, furnishings or personal belongings should be moved to a dry place if this can be done safely.

items.title: a burst pipe in winter
items.content: We may ask for evidence that the pipework was adequately maintained and protected against cold weather. This may include photographs, repair invoices, or confirmation of any temporary measures you took after discovering the leak.

items.title: a burst pipe in winter
items.content: Claims for escape of water may be reduced or declined where reasonable precautions were not taken. In particular, properties left unheated for long periods in winter are at greater risk of damage from frozen pipes.

items.title: a burst pipe in winter
items.content: You must not switch on electrical items or heating equipment if they have been affected by water from a burst pipe until they have been checked by a suitably qualified person. Safety must take priority over any attempt to restore normal use quickly.

items.title: a burst pipe in winter
items.content: If the burst pipe has caused damage to ceilings, walls or flooring, please make temporary repairs only where necessary to prevent further harm. Permanent repairs should be carried out by an appropriate tradesperson once the cause has been identified and dealt with.

items.title: a burst pipe in winter
items.content: Larkmere Mutual will normally consider the cost of locating the source of the escape and repairing resultant damage, subject to the terms of the policy. We do not usually cover the cost of replacing the defective pipe itself unless the wording of your policy says otherwise.

items.title: a leaking washing machine damaging the floor
items.content: If a washing machine leaks and water damages the floor, we will normally treat this as escape of water, provided the loss was sudden and accidental. Cover depends on the terms of the policy, including the cause of the leak and whether the property was adequately maintained. You should take reasonable steps to stop further damage as soon as it is safe to do so.

items.title: a leaking washing machine damaging the floor
items.content: Where water from a leaking appliance has affected flooring, we may consider the age, type and condition of the floor when deciding the claim. Wear and tear, gradual seepage and lack of maintenance are not covered causes. We may also ask for photographs and evidence of the source of the leak.

items.title: a leaking washing machine damaging the floor
items.content: If the washing machine overflowed because of a fault, damage caused by the escaping water may be covered under the home policy. Damage to the appliance itself is not usually covered unless a specific section of cover applies. Any excess shown in your schedule will be deducted from the settlement.

items.title: a leaking washing machine damaging the floor
items.content: We expect members to turn off the water supply if it can be done safely and to arrange emergency mitigation without delay. This helps reduce the extent of damage to floors, underlay and adjacent fittings. Failure to take reasonable care may affect the outcome of the claim.

items.title: a leaking washing machine damaging the floor
items.content: When a leak from a washing machine damages a wooden floor, we may need to inspect whether the boards can be dried and restored or whether replacement is necessary. We will not pay to improve the flooring beyond its pre-loss condition. Matching of undamaged areas is subject to the policy wording and the limits of indemnity.

items.title: a leaking washing machine damaging the floor
items.content: Escape of water claims are assessed on the basis of direct physical loss or damage. If the leak was gradual, or if the floor was already deteriorating, the resulting damage may not be covered. You must tell us as soon as reasonably possible after discovering the incident.

items.title: a leaking washing machine damaging the floor
items.content: Where water has soaked into a floor covering, carpet or laminate after a washing machine leak, we may settle the claim by repair, replacement or a cash payment at our discretion. We may choose the most cost-effective method that returns the damaged part to a reasonable condition. Any betterment may be taken into account.

items.title: a leaking washing machine damaging the floor
items.content: If the leak has affected a kitchen or utility room floor, we may also consider whether temporary drying equipment is needed. Reasonable costs to prevent further damage are generally included where they are agreed by us. You should keep receipts for emergency works and materials.

items.title: a leaking washing machine damaging the floor
items.content: Damage resulting from faulty installation may be covered only where the loss is caused by an insured event and not by a defect known before the start of cover. We may decline claims where the washing machine was improperly connected or maintained. Regular maintenance is the responsibility of the member.

items.title: a leaking washing machine damaging the floor
items.content: Our decision on a leaking washing machine claim will be based on the policy terms, the circumstances of the loss and any expert report we obtain. If flooring is beyond economic repair, we will consider a like-for-like replacement subject to policy limits and any applicable excess. Members may ask for a review if they believe the claim has been assessed incorrectly.

items.title: a leaking washing machine damaging the floor
items.content: If a washing machine suddenly leaks and causes water damage to the insured floor, we will consider the claim under escape of water cover, provided the loss was not gradual or caused by poor maintenance. Any damaged flooring will be assessed against the policy terms, limits and any applicable excess.

items.title: a leaking washing machine damaging the floor
items.content: You must take reasonable steps to stop further damage once a leak is discovered. This includes turning off the water supply where safe to do so and arranging prompt repairs to the appliance before it is used again.

items.title: a leaking washing machine damaging the floor
items.content: Damage resulting from wear and tear, deterioration, or a fault that developed over time is not covered. We may decline a claim where the washing machine was not kept in proper working order or where the leak was foreseeable.

items.title: a leaking washing machine damaging the floor
items.content: Where a leak from a washing machine has affected only part of a floor, we will normally look to repair the damaged area rather than replace the whole floor, unless matching cannot reasonably be achieved. Any decision on replacement will depend on the extent of the damage and the availability of suitable materials.

items.title: a leak from the flat upstairs
items.content: Where water has leaked from a flat above yours, you should take immediate steps to protect the property and prevent further damage. This includes moving items away from the affected area, containing the leak where possible, and reporting the incident as soon as reasonably practicable.

items.title: a leak from the flat upstairs
items.content: A leak from an upstairs flat may be the responsibility of the person in occupation or of the freeholder, depending on the cause of the escape of water. We may ask you to provide details of the source of the leak and any managing agent or landlord involvement before we can assess the claim.

items.title: a leak from the flat upstairs
items.content: If a leak from the flat above has caused damage to ceilings, walls, flooring or contents, we will consider the claim under the escape of water section of your policy, subject to the terms, limits and excesses that apply. You must not dispose of damaged items unless we have agreed this is appropriate or they present a health or safety risk.

items.title: a leak from the flat upstairs
items.content: You should notify the occupier above and, where appropriate, the building’s managing agent without delay so the source of the leak can be stopped. Failure to act promptly may increase the damage and could affect the amount we pay.

items.title: a leak from the flat upstairs
items.content: We may ask for evidence of the damage, including photographs, invoices and a brief account of when the leak started and when it was discovered. If a temporary repair is needed to prevent further damage, reasonable emergency costs may be considered in line with the policy.

items.title: a leak from the flat upstairs
items.content: Where water ingress has affected decorative finishes only, we will normally repair or replace the damaged part of the room rather than carry out a full match across undamaged areas, unless the policy wording states otherwise. Any settlement will reflect the condition, age and wear of the affected items.

items.title: a leak from the flat upstairs
items.content: If a leak from the flat upstairs is ongoing, you should arrange access to enable the source to be inspected and isolated as soon as possible. We will not normally pay for avoidable further damage where reasonable steps to reduce loss were not taken.

items.title: a leak from the flat upstairs
items.content: Damage caused by a sudden escape of water from an upper flat is usually covered, but wear and tear, poor maintenance or gradual seepage may not be. We will decide the claim by reference to the cause of the leak and the evidence available.

items.title: a leak from the flat upstairs
items.content: If the incident has led to mould, staining or deterioration of plaster, we may require drying and remedial work before permanent repairs are carried out. Any reinstatement must be reasonable and necessary to return the property to a habitable condition.

items.title: a leak from the flat upstairs
items.content: Where the leak originated in a neighbouring flat, any recovery action may be directed against the responsible party or their insurer. This does not affect your duty to notify us and to minimise loss under the policy.

items.title: a leak from the flat upstairs
items.content: If water has leaked from a flat above yours, you should take reasonable steps to limit further damage and report the matter to us as soon as practicable. We may ask you to provide photographs, details of where the water entered, and whether the source has been stopped.

items.title: a leak from the flat upstairs
items.content: Cover under this policy may respond to damage caused by escape of water from a neighbouring flat, subject to the terms, limits and exclusions of your policy schedule. This does not automatically include the cost of repairing the source of the leak in another property.

items.title: a leak from the flat upstairs
items.content: Where a leak from the flat upstairs has affected ceilings, walls or flooring, we will consider the resulting damage in accordance with the buildings or contents section that applies. Any deterioration caused by delay in reporting the incident may reduce the amount payable.

items.title: a leak from the flat upstairs
items.content: You should notify the owner, occupier or managing agent of the flat above as soon as possible, so that the source of the leak can be investigated and stopped. If the water continues to enter your home, we may arrange emergency mitigation to reduce further damage.

items.title: a break-in while on holiday
items.content: If your home is broken into while you are away on holiday, you must report the matter to the police as soon as reasonably practicable and obtain a crime reference number. You should also tell us promptly and give us full details of what was taken, how entry was gained, and when the loss was discovered.

items.title: a break-in while on holiday
items.content: For theft claims following a break-in, we may ask for evidence of ownership, purchase, or value for the items claimed. Where available, please provide photographs, receipts, serial numbers, or warranty documents to help us assess the claim.

items.title: a break-in while on holiday
items.content: If the burglary involved forced entry, please do not remove, repair, or discard damaged locks, doors, or windows until we have had the opportunity to inspect them, unless urgent safety measures are needed. Reasonable emergency repairs may be carried out to make the home secure, but keep any invoices and photographs.

items.title: a break-in while on holiday
items.content: Where a break-in occurs while the home is unoccupied for a holiday, the policy conditions on security and occupancy may apply. If any part of the property was left insecure, or if alarms and locks were not used as required, this may affect cover.

items.title: a break-in while on holiday
items.content: You should take reasonable steps to prevent further loss after a burglary, including securing the property and arranging temporary protection where needed. We may reimburse reasonable costs for emergency make-safe work if these are covered under your policy and are supported by evidence.

items.title: a break-in while on holiday
items.content: If keys, fobs, or access codes were taken during the break-in, you must tell us without delay. You are expected to arrange replacement or reprogramming where necessary, as continued use of compromised access devices may increase the risk of further loss.

items.title: a break-in while on holiday
items.content: When you return from holiday, check the home carefully for signs of entry, missing items, and any damage to the building. Tell us about all related losses in one claim where possible, including damage caused by the intruder and theft of contents or personal belongings.

items.title: a break-in while on holiday
items.content: Certain valuable items may have special limits, conditions, or requirements for proof of ownership under the policy. If such items are stolen in a break-in, the amount payable may be restricted unless the relevant cover and security conditions were met.

items.title: a break-in while on holiday
items.content: We will consider each burglary claim on the information provided and any evidence we can obtain from the police, repairers, or other relevant parties. If there is any discrepancy about the circumstances of the break-in, we may ask further questions before deciding the claim.

items.title: a break-in while on holiday
items.content: If the break-in results in temporary loss of use of the home, any cover for alternative accommodation will depend on the terms of your policy. We will only pay reasonable additional costs that are necessary as a direct result of insured damage and while the property is being made secure.

items.title: a break-in while on holiday
items.content: If your home is burgled whilst you are away on holiday, you must report the incident to the police as soon as possible and obtain a crime reference number. Please tell us without delay and provide the details we reasonably ask for so we can assess your claim.

items.title: a break-in while on holiday
items.content: For theft following a break-in, cover applies only where there is clear evidence of forcible and violent entry or exit. You must take reasonable steps to secure the property once the loss is discovered.

items.title: a break-in while on holiday
items.content: Where keys have been taken in a burglary, we may pay the reasonable cost of changing locks or reprogramming security devices if the theft occurred during an insured event. Cover is subject to the limits shown in your schedule and policy wording.

items.title: a break-in while on holiday
items.content: If you are on holiday and discover that your home has been broken into, you should arrange for a responsible person to check the property where safe to do so. You must not enter a property if you believe intruders may still be inside, and you should contact the police immediately.

items.title: a bike stolen from the garden
items.content: If a bicycle is stolen from your garden, you must tell us as soon as reasonably possible and report the theft to the police. We may ask for the crime reference number, proof of ownership and photographs or purchase records, where available.

items.title: a bike stolen from the garden
items.content: Cover for theft from a garden only applies where the bicycle was secured in accordance with the policy conditions. If the bicycle was left unsecured, or the security requirements were not met, we may not be able to pay the claim.

items.title: a bike stolen from the garden
items.content: For theft from outbuildings or gardens, we expect reasonable care to have been taken to protect the bicycle from loss. This may include locking it to an immovable object or keeping it within a locked shed or garage.

items.title: a bike stolen from the garden
items.content: We will consider a claim for a bicycle stolen from the garden only if the loss happened during the period of insurance and at the insured address. Any item removed with your consent is not a theft for the purposes of this cover.

items.title: a bike stolen from the garden
items.content: You should keep evidence of the bicycle’s value and any identifying marks or frame number. If the bicycle is recovered after payment, it becomes our property unless we agree otherwise.

items.title: a bike stolen from the garden
items.content: Theft from a garden is not covered where the loss results from a malicious or dishonest act by a member of your household. We may also decline the claim if there is evidence that the bicycle was left in a place visible and readily accessible to thieves contrary to the policy terms.

items.title: a bike stolen from the garden
items.content: Where a bicycle is stolen from the garden, we may settle the claim by repair, replacement or cash payment at our option. Any payment will be based on the policy limits, excess and the condition of the bicycle immediately before the loss.

items.title: a bike stolen from the garden
items.content: You must take all reasonable steps to prevent further loss after the theft. If replacement keys, locks or security devices are needed because the bicycle was stolen from the garden, we will only consider them where the policy expressly provides cover.

items.title: a bike stolen from the garden
items.content: If the bicycle was attached to garden furniture, fencing or another fixed structure, we will look at whether the attachment met the security standard shown in your schedule or wording. Failure to meet that standard may affect the amount we pay, or whether we pay at all.

items.title: a bike stolen from the garden
items.content: We may ask for additional evidence where the circumstances of the garden theft are unclear, including witness details, photographs of the scene and proof that the bicycle was kept at the property. Any false or exaggerated claim may result in cancellation of cover and refusal of payment.

items.title: a bike stolen from the garden
items.content: If your bicycle is stolen from the garden, cover applies only where the garden is part of the home premises and reasonable care has been taken to secure the property. You must report the theft to the police promptly and obtain a crime reference number. We may also ask for proof of ownership and purchase value.

items.title: a bike stolen from the garden
items.content: Bicycles left in an open garden are not covered unless the policy expressly includes theft from outbuildings or enclosed private grounds. Any claim may be reduced or declined if the bicycle was left unsecured or in a place readily accessible from outside the boundary. Locks, chains and stored items are expected to be used in a sensible manner.

items.title: a bike stolen from the garden
items.content: Where theft from the garden is covered, the bicycle must have been locked to a fixed object or secured within a locked shed, garage or similar outbuilding. We do not consider a simple presence within the garden, by itself, to be adequate security. Evidence of forced entry may be requested where the item was kept in an enclosed structure.

items.title: a bike stolen from the garden
items.content: You should notify us as soon as possible after discovering the theft, and no later than the time limit set out in your policy booklet. Delay in reporting may affect our ability to verify the circumstances of the loss. We may also ask whether the incident was reported to the police on the same day.

items.title: a stolen card used abroad
items.content: If your card is lost or stolen and then used abroad, you must tell us as soon as you can by calling the number shown in your account documents. We may ask you to confirm the date and circumstances of the loss or theft, and to cancel the card immediately to reduce the risk of further misuse.

items.title: a stolen card used abroad
items.content: We will review unauthorised transactions on a stolen card used outside the UK in line with our cardholder terms. Where you have taken reasonable care of the card and PIN, you will not usually be liable for losses after you have notified us, except where the law allows otherwise.

items.title: a stolen card used abroad
items.content: If a card is reported stolen, we may place a block on all cash withdrawals and purchases, including those attempted abroad. This block may remain in place until we have completed our security checks and issued a replacement card where appropriate.

items.title: a stolen card used abroad
items.content: Transactions made abroad may be authorised in local currency and later converted into sterling. Where a stolen card has been used overseas, the amount refunded may therefore differ slightly from the original transaction value because of exchange rate movements and card network adjustments.

items.title: a stolen card used abroad
items.content: You should keep any police crime reference number if the card was stolen, particularly where the theft occurred overseas. We may ask for this evidence when investigating disputed card transactions or when considering reimbursement.

items.title: a stolen card used abroad
items.content: A cash withdrawal made abroad with a stolen card may be treated differently from a purchase transaction if a PIN was used. If we believe the PIN was disclosed or not kept secure, we may ask further questions before deciding whether the transaction is covered.

items.title: a stolen card used abroad
items.content: Where a stolen card used abroad has been linked to repeated transactions, we may treat the matter as a security incident and issue a new card number. Any recurring payments taken after the card was reported stolen will be dealt with under the relevant payment rules.

items.title: a stolen card used abroad
items.content: We may refuse reimbursement for a transaction where we reasonably believe the card, PIN or security details were not protected in accordance with our terms. This includes leaving the card unattended, recording the PIN with the card, or otherwise failing to take reasonable precautions.

items.title: a stolen card used abroad
items.content: If you are abroad when you discover the card has been stolen, you should contact us without delay and, where possible, use the emergency contact details in your card pack. We will then explain the steps available to protect your account and arrange a replacement card if eligible.

items.title: a stolen card used abroad
items.content: Our investigation will consider the time the card was stolen, when it was used abroad and when you notified us. If the transactions were unauthorised and reported promptly, we will usually correct your account once our checks are complete.

items.title: a stolen card used abroad
items.content: If your card is lost or stolen, you must tell us straight away so we can cancel it and protect your account. If you notice transactions you do not recognise, you should contact us without delay, even if the card has already been blocked. We may ask you to confirm the time and place the card went missing.

items.title: a stolen card used abroad
items.content: Where a card is used abroad before you report it missing, you may be liable for some or all of the resulting losses if you have acted fraudulently or with gross negligence. We will consider the circumstances of each case, including how promptly you notified us and whether the card and PIN were kept safely. Any decision on liability will be made in line with the card terms and applicable law.

items.title: a stolen card used abroad
items.content: Transactions carried out in a foreign country may appear on your statement in the local currency and then be converted to sterling. The amount shown may include a card scheme exchange rate and a foreign transaction fee, where applicable. These charges are not removed simply because the card was later reported stolen.

items.title: a stolen card used abroad
items.content: If we suspect the card has been used fraudulently abroad, we may contact you to verify recent transactions. We may also place a temporary restriction on the card or account while we investigate. This is to reduce further misuse and protect your funds.

items.title: cracks appearing in the walls
items.content: If cracks appear in external or internal walls, members should report them to Larkmere Mutual without delay and take photographs showing their location and extent. Small cracks caused by minor settlement may be monitored, but any widening, diagonal or stepped cracking, or cracking that appears suddenly should be assessed promptly by a suitable professional. We may ask for further evidence before deciding whether the damage is covered.

items.title: cracks appearing in the walls
items.content: Cracks that are consistent with subsidence, heave or landslip must be notified as soon as they are discovered. Members should avoid carrying out repairs, making alterations or removing nearby trees until Larkmere Mutual has reviewed the circumstances, as this may affect our ability to investigate the cause. We may arrange a survey or request a report from an approved engineer.

items.title: cracks appearing in the walls
items.content: Where cracks are reported, our first step is to consider whether the damage is cosmetic or whether it may indicate movement affecting the structure. Cracks wider than hairline, particularly those around doors, windows, ceilings or extensions, may require urgent inspection. If there is any sign of unsafe movement, the member should not use the affected area until it has been checked.

items.title: cracks appearing in the walls
items.content: Larkmere Mutual does not expect members to undertake invasive investigation of cracks themselves. Any opening up of walls, floors or finishes should only be carried out with our agreement, unless immediate action is required to make the home safe. We may decline cover for unnecessary work completed before we have had a reasonable opportunity to inspect the damage.

items.title: cracks appearing in the walls
items.content: Cracking caused by building works, poor workmanship or gradual wear and tear is not covered under the buildings section of the policy. However, if the cracking is accompanied by a one-off insured event, such as storm damage or impact, the claim will be considered in line with the policy wording. Members should provide dates, details of any works and any relevant contractor information.

items.title: cracks appearing in the walls
items.content: Where cracks are linked to an escape of water, members must stop the leak if it is safe to do so and notify us promptly. We may cover resulting damage to walls, plaster and decoration, subject to the terms, limits and exclusions of the policy. Ongoing dampness or repeated seepage will be treated differently from sudden and accidental damage.

items.title: cracks appearing in the walls
items.content: If cracks are found in boundary walls, retaining walls or outbuildings, the member should report them and describe any nearby ground movement, drainage issues or tree roots. These features can help establish whether the damage is related to an insured peril or to gradual causes. We may ask for ownership details and evidence of maintenance.

items.title: remortgaging at the end of a fixed rate
items.content: At the end of a fixed rate period, the account will automatically revert to our variable reversion rate unless you have agreed a new product in advance. Members are responsible for making sure any remortgage application is submitted in good time if they wish to avoid moving onto the reversion rate. We will write to you before the fixed rate ends to explain your options.

items.title: remortgaging at the end of a fixed rate
items.content: Where a member wishes to remortgage into a new Larkmere Mutual product, the application must be completed and approved before the existing fixed rate expires. If completion takes place after the end date, the account may move onto the standard variable rate for the intervening period. Any new interest rate will apply only from the date agreed in the offer.

items.title: remortgaging at the end of a fixed rate
items.content: We may require an updated valuation, income evidence and a review of your current mortgage conduct before approving a remortgage at the end of a fixed rate. The amount you can borrow will depend on our lending criteria at the time of application. Borrowing terms may differ from those that applied when the original mortgage was taken out.

items.title: remortgaging at the end of a fixed rate
items.content: If you are moving to another lender at the end of a fixed rate, you remain responsible for ensuring that redemption funds are available on the completion date. Early repayment charges may apply if you repay the mortgage before the fixed rate ends or outside any permitted transfer window. Your offer will confirm whether such charges apply.

items.title: remortgaging at the end of a fixed rate
items.content: A remortgage application does not guarantee that the fixed rate will be extended or replaced with another fixed rate. We reserve the right to decline an application where affordability, credit or property criteria are not met. If declined, your mortgage will continue on the terms then in force, including any reversion rate where applicable.

items.title: remortgaging at the end of a fixed rate
items.content: Members should contact us as soon as they receive notice that their fixed rate is ending if they intend to remortgage. We cannot be responsible for delays caused by incomplete information, missing documents or late instructions from a broker or solicitor. It is your responsibility to allow sufficient time for the process to be completed.

items.title: remortgaging at the end of a fixed rate
items.content: Where a new product is arranged at the end of a fixed rate, the new payment amount may differ from the previous instalment. We will advise the revised monthly payment in your offer or product transfer confirmation. You should check that your direct debit mandate remains suitable for the new amount.

items.title: remortgaging at the end of a fixed rate
items.content: If you are capitalising fees as part of a remortgage, the total loan amount must remain within the maximum lending limits for the product selected. Fees may include valuation, legal and administration charges. Any fees we require you to pay must be settled in accordance with the instructions issued at offer stage.

items.title: remortgaging at the end of a fixed rate
items.content: A product transfer at the end of a fixed rate is subject to our current lending policy and may not be available on all mortgage accounts. Interest-only borrowing may require a separate review of the repayment strategy. We may ask for documentary evidence that the repayment plan remains adequate.

items.title: remortgaging at the end of a fixed rate
items.content: If the fixed rate ends and no new arrangement has completed, the mortgage will continue on the rate and terms shown in your mortgage conditions. You may still remortgage later, but the new rate will only take effect from the date of completion. Any overpayments or arrears will be taken into account when we assess the application.

items.title: remortgaging at the end of a fixed rate
items.content: At the end of a fixed rate term, your mortgage will usually move onto Larkmere Mutual’s reversionary variable rate unless you choose a new product in advance. We will write to you before the fixed rate ends to explain your options and any change to your monthly payment.

items.title: remortgaging at the end of a fixed rate
items.content: If you wish to remortgage on to a new fixed rate with Larkmere Mutual, you should complete your application before the current deal expires. Any new rate will take effect from the date agreed in your offer, and not before the end of the existing fixed rate period.

items.title: remortgaging at the end of a fixed rate
items.content: Customers may switch to another Larkmere Mutual mortgage product at the end of a fixed rate, subject to eligibility and the product available at the time. Early repayment charges may apply if the current deal has not yet ended when the switch is completed.

items.title: remortgaging at the end of a fixed rate
items.content: Where a fixed rate is ending, we will normally review your account to confirm the balance, term and any changes needed to your direct debit. If your payment is due to increase, we will show the revised amount before you make your choice.

items.title: remortgaging at the end of a fixed rate
items.content: A remortgage at the end of a fixed rate does not require a new property valuation in every case. We may request further checks where the loan amount, term or property details have changed, or where additional lending is requested.

items.title: remortgaging at the end of a fixed rate
items.content: If you are moving from a fixed rate to a new product with a shorter or longer term, the total amount payable may change even where the loan balance remains the same. You should consider your remaining term carefully before accepting a new rate.

items.title: remortgaging at the end of a fixed rate
items.content: An application to remortgage at the end of a fixed rate may be declined if the borrower no longer meets our lending criteria. In such cases, the account will usually revert to the standard variable rate when the current deal ends.

items.title: remortgaging at the end of a fixed rate
items.content: We recommend that members contact us before the last three months of the fixed rate term if they wish to discuss remortgaging options. This allows sufficient time for us to assess the application and issue an offer, where appropriate.

items.title: remortgaging at the end of a fixed rate
items.content: If you choose not to arrange a new mortgage product, your current monthly payment may not cover the full amount due under the reversionary rate. You remain responsible for ensuring payments are made on time and in full after the fixed rate has ended.

items.title: remortgaging at the end of a fixed rate
items.content: Any fee payable for switching to a new mortgage product will be set out in the offer and product information sheet. We will not complete a remortgage until any applicable fee arrangements and required documentation have been accepted.

items.title: remortgaging at the end of a fixed rate
items.content: At the end of a fixed rate period, the account will normally revert to the Society’s standard variable rate unless a new product is arranged in advance. Members should review their options before the fixed term expires to avoid an unplanned change in monthly payments.

items.title: overpaying the mortgage
items.content: You may make overpayments to reduce the balance of your mortgage, subject to the terms of your mortgage offer and any applicable limits. Overpayments will ordinarily be applied first to outstanding interest and then to capital, unless your mortgage conditions state otherwise.

items.title: overpaying the mortgage
items.content: If you wish to make a lump-sum overpayment, you must ensure that cleared funds are available before the payment date. Any overpayment received after the contractual payment date may not reduce the next monthly instalment.

items.title: overpaying the mortgage
items.content: Some mortgage products allow regular overpayments by standing order or additional ad hoc payments. Where an early repayment charge applies, overpayments above the permitted allowance may result in a charge under your mortgage conditions.

items.title: overpaying the mortgage
items.content: Overpaying your mortgage may reduce the total interest payable over the term and may shorten the remaining term. It may also affect the amount of any future final payment, where your account is arranged on an interest-only basis.

items.title: overpaying the mortgage
items.content: You should not treat overpayments as a substitute for maintaining your required monthly payment. If your account falls into arrears, we may use any overpayment balance to reduce the arrears before applying it to capital reduction.

items.title: overpaying the mortgage
items.content: If you have a joint mortgage, either borrower may make an overpayment unless your mortgage agreement requires us to act on all borrowers' instructions. We may ask for additional confirmation where the payment arrangement is unusual or where fraud prevention checks are required.

items.title: overpaying the mortgage
items.content: Overpayments do not always alter your contractual monthly payment automatically. Unless we agree to recalculate your direct debit, your normal payment amount may remain unchanged and the term may be reduced instead.

items.title: overpaying the mortgage
items.content: Where your mortgage is close to redemption, you should contact us before making an overpayment so that we can provide an accurate settlement figure. An overpayment made without prior notice may not be sufficient to redeem the account in full.

items.title: overpaying the mortgage
items.content: If a refund becomes due following an overpayment, we will normally return the excess to the originating bank account. We do not usually hold overpayments on account unless this is permitted by your mortgage product and you request it.

items.title: overpaying the mortgage
items.content: Any overpayment made after the mortgage has been redeemed may be treated as a mistaken payment. In those circumstances, we will investigate the payment and arrange a refund where appropriate, subject to our standard checks.

items.title: overpaying the mortgage
items.content: You may make overpayments on your Larkmere Mutual mortgage at any time, subject to the terms of your mortgage offer. Overpayments will reduce the outstanding balance and may shorten the mortgage term, but they do not replace your scheduled monthly payment unless we agree otherwise in writing.

items.title: overpaying the mortgage
items.content: Where your mortgage product allows overpayments, the maximum amount may be limited to a percentage of the outstanding balance each year. Any amount above the permitted allowance may incur an early repayment charge, as set out in your mortgage conditions.

items.title: overpaying the mortgage
items.content: If you choose to overpay by card or bank transfer, the payment must be cleared funds and received on a business day to be applied promptly. Payments received after the monthly collection date may be credited to your account but not treated as an arrears cure unless we confirm this to you.

items.title: overpaying the mortgage
items.content: You should keep your monthly direct debit in place unless we have confirmed an amended payment arrangement. Making an overpayment does not, by itself, alter the amount or date of your next scheduled instalment.

items.title: a complaint about a slow claim
items.content: If you are unhappy with the time taken to progress your claim, you may raise a complaint at any stage. We will acknowledge it promptly and set out the next steps for review. Your complaint will be handled separately from the claim itself where appropriate.

items.title: a complaint about a slow claim
items.content: We will provide a clear update on the status of your claim when a delay has occurred. Where further investigation is needed, we will explain what is outstanding and the likely timescale for completion. We aim to keep you informed until the matter is resolved.

items.title: a complaint about a slow claim
items.content: A complaint about delay will be reviewed by a member of staff who was not directly involved in the original handling where this is reasonably practicable. They will consider the information already held on the claim and any additional points you provide. This helps us assess whether our service has fallen below the standard you should expect.

items.title: a complaint about a slow claim
items.content: If we require documents, reports or third-party information before a claim can be settled, we will tell you why the claim remains open. We will also let you know whether the delay is within our control or depends on another party. We will not leave you without explanation for avoidable periods.

items.title: a complaint about a slow claim
items.content: Where a complaint concerns a slow claim, we will check whether our service standards, communication and diary management were followed. If we find that our handling contributed to unnecessary delay, we will consider an appropriate remedy. This may include a written apology and any further action needed to put matters right.

items.title: a complaint about a slow claim
items.content: You may ask us to review a claim that has remained unresolved for an unreasonably long time. We will examine the reasons for the delay and whether any additional information is required from you. If the claim cannot be settled immediately, we will provide a revised action plan.

items.title: a complaint about a slow claim
items.content: Our procedure requires us to respond to complaint points about delay in plain language and without technical wording where possible. We will set out what has happened, what we are doing now and when you can expect the next update. We will not use a standard reply that fails to address your specific concerns.

items.title: a complaint about a slow claim
items.content: A complaint about slow claims handling does not affect your right to pursue the underlying claim under your policy. If the complaint is upheld, the claim will continue to be progressed under the relevant policy terms. Any remedy for poor service will be considered separately from the claim outcome.

items.title: a complaint about a slow claim
items.content: We recognise that prolonged uncertainty can be frustrating, especially where repairs, replacement or temporary arrangements are affected. For that reason, we aim to deal with complaints about delay as a matter of priority. We will take the circumstances of your claim into account when deciding how urgently a review is needed.

items.title: a complaint about a slow claim
items.content: If you remain dissatisfied after our final response, you may be entitled to refer the complaint to the Financial Ombudsman Service. We will explain this right in our final response letter and provide the time limits that apply. This ensures you know your options if our review does not resolve the matter.

items.title: a complaint about a slow claim
items.content: If a claim is progressing more slowly than expected, members should contact the claims team so we can review the file and explain any outstanding steps. We will tell the member what information we still need and when they can expect the next update.

items.title: a complaint about a slow claim
items.content: We aim to handle claims promptly and fairly, but some cases take longer where further evidence, contractor availability or third-party enquiries are required. A delay does not mean the claim will be refused.

items.title: a complaint about a slow claim
items.content: Where a claim has become delayed, we will keep the member informed at appropriate intervals and set out the reason for the delay in clear terms. We will also confirm any action we are taking to move the claim on.

items.title: a complaint about a slow claim
items.content: A complaint about slow handling of a claim will be logged and investigated under our complaints procedure. We will consider whether our service fell below the standard the member could reasonably expect.

items.title: a declined claim the member disputes
items.content: If we decline a claim, we will explain our reasons in writing and refer you to the relevant terms and conditions of your policy. You may ask us to review the decision if you believe we have misunderstood the facts or applied the policy incorrectly. Any request for review should be made as soon as reasonably possible after you receive our decision.

items.title: a declined claim the member disputes
items.content: When you dispute a declined claim, we will re-examine the claim file, including the information you supplied, any expert reports, and the policy wording in force at the time of the loss. If further information may affect the outcome, we may ask you to provide it before we complete the review. Our decision on review will be confirmed in writing.

items.title: a declined claim the member disputes
items.content: A claim may be declined where the event is not covered, the policy terms have not been met, or the loss falls within an exclusion. We will set out which part of the policy applies and explain how it applies to your circumstances. Where appropriate, we will also tell you what evidence we relied upon.

items.title: a declined claim the member disputes
items.content: If you remain unhappy after our final response, you may be entitled to refer the matter to the Financial Ombudsman Service. We will tell you whether your complaint is eligible and, if so, how to contact the service. This does not affect your legal rights.

items.title: a declined claim the member disputes
items.content: We may decline a claim if there is insufficient evidence to support the cause, amount, or timing of the loss. Where the claim is disputed, we will consider any additional photographs, invoices, witness accounts, or inspection findings you provide. However, we are not able to accept evidence that does not reasonably support the claim made.

items.title: a declined claim the member disputes
items.content: If our decision turns on a condition precedent or a policy condition, we will identify the condition and explain the consequence of non-compliance. In some cases, we may still pay part of the claim where the breach did not affect the loss or our ability to investigate it. Each case is assessed on its own facts.

items.title: a declined claim the member disputes
items.content: We will handle any disagreement about a declined claim fairly, promptly and with due regard to the principle of treating members consistently. Where a technical issue is involved, we may obtain a second opinion from a suitably qualified assessor. We will not alter a decision without a proper basis in the policy or the evidence.

items.title: a declined claim the member disputes
items.content: If you think a claim has been declined in error, you should tell us which part of the decision you dispute and why. Clear and specific information helps us review the matter efficiently. We may uphold, vary, or overturn the original decision after review.

items.title: a declined claim the member disputes
items.content: A dispute about a declined claim does not extend cover beyond what your policy provides. Even where a loss feels unfair, we can only pay claims that meet the cover, limits, and conditions agreed. Our role is to apply the policy wording to the facts of the claim.

items.title: a declined claim the member disputes
items.content: Where a decline is based on an exclusion, we will quote the exclusion or summarise it accurately and explain why it applies. If the wording is ambiguous, we will interpret it consistently with the overall policy and relevant legal principles. Any doubt will be considered against the full facts of the claim and the evidence available.

items.title: a declined claim the member disputes
items.content: If we decline a claim, we will explain the reasons for our decision in writing and refer you to the relevant policy terms. You may ask us to review the claim if you believe we have misunderstood the circumstances or applied the policy incorrectly.

items.title: a declined claim the member disputes
items.content: A dispute about a declined claim should be raised with us as soon as possible and, where practical, with any supporting documents you hold. We will reconsider the claim in light of any additional information you provide.

items.title: a declined claim the member disputes
items.content: Where a claim remains declined after review, we will issue a final response setting out our position clearly. That response will tell you whether you have the right to refer the matter to the Financial Ombudsman Service.

items.title: a declined claim the member disputes
items.content: We may ask for further evidence before completing our review, including photographs, invoices, repair estimates, or correspondence relevant to the loss. A review will only proceed on the basis of the facts available and the terms and conditions of the policy.

items.title: going to the Financial Ombudsman
items.content: If you remain dissatisfied after we have sent our final response, you may be entitled to refer your complaint to the Financial Ombudsman Service. You must usually do so within six months of the date of our final response. The Ombudsman service is free to use.

items.title: going to the Financial Ombudsman
items.content: We will tell you in our final response whether your complaint may be taken to the Financial Ombudsman Service. This will include the time limit for bringing your complaint to them. If you do not refer your complaint within the stated time, the Ombudsman may not be able to consider it.

items.title: going to the Financial Ombudsman
items.content: The Financial Ombudsman Service is independent and will look at complaints in a fair and impartial way. It can review the circumstances of your case and decide what is appropriate. Its decision may be binding on us if you accept it.

items.title: going to the Financial Ombudsman
items.content: You should contact us first so that we have the opportunity to investigate and respond to your concerns. If we are unable to resolve matters to your satisfaction, you may then ask the Financial Ombudsman Service to review the complaint. We will provide you with the relevant contact details on request.

items.title: going to the Financial Ombudsman
items.content: If your complaint concerns the outcome of a claim or a policy decision, the Financial Ombudsman Service may ask for evidence of our final response. Please keep copies of all letters, emails and other correspondence. This will help the Ombudsman understand what has happened.

items.title: going to the Financial Ombudsman
items.content: Where we issue a final response, we will explain our reasons and set out any offer we have made. If you do not accept the outcome, you may be able to take the matter to the Financial Ombudsman Service. The Ombudsman will decide whether it can consider the complaint under its rules.

items.title: going to the Financial Ombudsman
items.content: The Financial Ombudsman Service can consider many complaints from personal customers and eligible micro-enterprises. It cannot usually deal with a matter until you have given us the chance to put it right. We will work with you in good faith during our complaints process before any referral is made.

items.title: whether the home policy covers flooding
items.content: Flood damage is covered under the home policy unless a specific exclusion or endorsement says otherwise. We will assess each claim against the terms, limits and conditions that apply to the policy in force at the time of the loss.

items.title: whether the home policy covers flooding
items.content: If water enters the home as a result of flooding, the policy may respond where flood cover is included in your chosen level of cover. Flood is treated as an insured peril and is not covered where the policy schedule states that flood cover has been removed.

items.title: whether the home policy covers flooding
items.content: Our home insurance does not provide unlimited flood cover. Claims arising from flood are subject to the policy excess, any special terms shown on the schedule, and the duty to take reasonable steps to reduce further damage.

items.title: whether the home policy covers flooding
items.content: Flood may include surface water, river overflow, tidal inundation and water escaping from defences after exceptional weather. Where the event falls within the policy definition of flood, we will consider the claim in line with that definition.

items.title: whether the home policy covers flooding
items.content: We expect members to tell us promptly if their home has been affected by flood, even where the immediate damage appears minor. Early notification helps us arrange assistance and prevent avoidable deterioration to the property.

items.title: whether the home policy covers flooding
items.content: Damage caused by flood is normally covered for the buildings and contents sections of the home policy, subject to the cover selected. However, contents taken outside the home are only covered if the policy wording specifically extends flood cover to those items.

items.title: whether the home policy covers flooding
items.content: The policy may exclude loss where flooding results from wear and tear, poor maintenance or defective workmanship that a reasonable householder should have addressed. In those circumstances, the flood itself may be the visible cause, but the underlying cause will determine whether cover applies.

items.title: waiting for the loss adjuster
items.content: If we appoint a loss adjuster, you must wait for their visit before carrying out permanent repairs, unless urgent action is needed to make the home safe or prevent further damage. We may ask you to preserve any damaged items and keep them available for inspection. Temporary protective measures are allowed where they are reasonably necessary.

items.title: waiting for the loss adjuster
items.content: Please do not dispose of damaged property until we or our loss adjuster have had the opportunity to inspect it. Photographs, receipts and any contractor quotations should be retained for our review. Where items must be discarded for safety reasons, please keep a clear record of what was removed.

items.title: waiting for the loss adjuster
items.content: If a loss adjuster is instructed, they will contact you to arrange an appointment. You should be ready to provide access to the affected rooms, loft, outbuildings and any other areas relevant to the claim. Delays in arranging access may slow our assessment and settlement of the claim.

items.title: waiting for the loss adjuster
items.content: You should continue to take reasonable steps to prevent further loss while waiting for the loss adjuster. This may include turning off water, boarding broken openings or moving undamaged possessions to a dry place. Such steps do not amount to acceptance of liability by us.

items.title: waiting for the loss adjuster
items.content: Do not instruct major repair work until the loss adjuster has inspected the damage and we have confirmed the next steps. If you need emergency repairs to make the property secure, please keep the work to what is strictly necessary. Any wider reinstatement should wait for our authorisation.

items.title: waiting for the loss adjuster
items.content: The loss adjuster will usually record the cause, extent and likely cost of the damage. You must provide honest and complete information and answer any reasonable questions they ask. If further specialist reports are needed, we may defer settlement until those reports are received.

items.title: waiting for the loss adjuster
items.content: Where there is a risk of mould, contamination or structural instability, you should wait for guidance from the loss adjuster before disturbing the affected area further. We may permit limited drying, cleaning or stabilisation where this is necessary to reduce the loss. Any such work should be proportionate and documented.

items.title: waiting for the loss adjuster
items.content: If we agree that you may proceed before the loss adjuster attends, that agreement will be limited to the specific work described. It does not mean that all costs will be accepted. You remain responsible for ensuring the work is reasonable and properly evidenced.

items.title: waiting for the loss adjuster
items.content: You must tell us promptly if the loss adjuster cannot gain access on the arranged date. We may need to reschedule and, where repeated delays occur, we may ask you to contact us to explain the reason. Failure to cooperate may affect the handling of the claim.

items.title: waiting for the loss adjuster
items.content: Once the loss adjuster has inspected the damage, they may ask for further information before we decide the claim. Please keep any quotations, invoices and correspondence until the claim is fully resolved. Waiting for inspection and further instructions helps us assess the loss fairly and accurately.

items.title: waiting for the loss adjuster
items.content: If we appoint a loss adjuster, please wait for them to contact you before arranging permanent repairs. They may need to inspect the damage, take photographs, and confirm the cause and extent of the loss. Delaying repairs until that visit helps us assess your claim fairly.

items.title: waiting for the loss adjuster
items.content: You should keep the damaged property in its current state wherever it is safe to do so, until the loss adjuster has attended. If urgent steps are needed to make the home secure or prevent further damage, you may take those steps first. Please keep any receipts and tell us what you have done.

items.title: waiting for the loss adjuster
items.content: The loss adjuster may need access to all affected rooms, contents, and any areas where water, smoke, or storm damage has travelled. If you are not available when the visit is arranged, let us know as soon as possible so that a new appointment can be made. Repeated missed appointments may delay progress on the claim.

items.title: waiting for the loss adjuster
items.content: Do not throw away damaged items before the loss adjuster has had the opportunity to inspect them, unless there is a health or safety reason to do so. Where disposal is unavoidable, please take clear photographs and retain samples if possible. This helps us understand what was lost and what can be settled.

items.title: waiting for the loss adjuster
items.content: If a contractor has already attended to carry out emergency work, please tell the loss adjuster what was done and when. The loss adjuster will usually want to see the damage before any full repair starts, unless we have agreed otherwise. Their report forms part of our decision on your claim.

items.title: waiting for the loss adjuster
items.content: While you are waiting for the loss adjuster, please continue to protect the property from further damage. This may include switching off water, covering broken windows, or moving belongings to a dry area. Such temporary measures do not count as a permanent repair.

items.title: waiting for the loss adjuster
items.content: The loss adjuster acts on our behalf to gather information about the claim and may ask questions about how the loss happened. Please answer as fully and accurately as you can. If you have photographs, invoices, or police references, have them ready for the visit or send them when requested.

items.title: waiting for the loss adjuster
items.content: If the loss adjuster needs specialist inspection, such as for subsidence, escape of water, or hidden structural damage, the claim may remain open for longer. In those cases, please wait for our instruction before authorising further work. We will keep you informed of any next steps.

items.title: waiting for the loss adjuster
items.content: We may ask you to provide dates, measurements, serial numbers, or proof of purchase before the loss adjuster attends. Having this information ready can help the visit proceed smoothly. It also helps us consider any items that may need replacement on a like-for-like basis.

items.title: waiting for the loss adjuster
items.content: If you have made a temporary arrangement to live elsewhere, please tell the loss adjuster during their visit. They will need to understand the extent of the damage and whether the home remains safe and habitable. We will then consider the claim in line with the cover in force.

items.title: waiting for the loss adjuster
items.content: If we appoint a loss adjuster, please wait for them to contact you before carrying out any permanent repairs. They may need to inspect the damage, gather evidence and agree the next steps with you. You should, however, take reasonable temporary measures to prevent further loss or damage.

items.title: chasing a contractor for repairs
items.content: Where repairs are arranged by Larkmere Mutual, the appointed contractor will be chased by our claims team on the member’s behalf if work is not progressing within the agreed timescale. We will record each contact attempt and seek a revised completion date where appropriate. If delay continues, we may review whether an alternative repair route is required.

items.title: chasing a contractor for repairs
items.content: Members should not repeatedly contact the contractor directly unless asked to do so by our claims handler. We will make the formal request for progress and remind the contractor of any agreed appointments. This helps us keep one clear record of the repair position.

items.title: chasing a contractor for repairs
items.content: If a contractor misses an appointment or fails to respond, we will seek an explanation and ask for immediate re-booking. Our team may escalate the matter to the contractor’s management where service standards are not being met. We will keep the member informed of any material delay.

items.title: chasing a contractor for repairs
items.content: We will chase a contractor where materials have been ordered but no start date has been confirmed. In such cases, we will ask for an expected delivery date and any impact on the repair schedule. If the contractor cannot progress the works, we may consider replacement arrangements.

items.title: chasing a contractor for repairs
items.content: When repairs are urgent, we will contact the contractor promptly and ask for the earliest available attendance. If the contractor cannot attend within a reasonable period, we may authorise another suitable contractor. Our priority is to reduce further damage and restore the property as soon as reasonably possible.

items.title: chasing a contractor for repairs
items.content: Where a repair has stalled, our claims handler will issue a reminder to the contractor and request written confirmation of next steps. If no satisfactory response is received, the case may be referred for internal review. We do not regard silence from a contractor as progress.

items.title: chasing a contractor for repairs
items.content: We may chase a contractor for photographs, completion notes or certification before closing a repair. This is necessary to confirm that the work has been carried out properly and safely. Until the required information is received, the claim record may remain open.

items.title: chasing a contractor for repairs
items.content: If a contractor advises that access is needed, we will ask the member to provide reasonable availability and will continue to monitor the appointment booking. Where access has already been given and the contractor still has not attended, we will pursue the matter directly. Delays caused by poor coordination are not accepted without explanation.

items.title: chasing a contractor for repairs
items.content: Our policy is to pursue regular updates from any contractor instructed by us on a claim. Members may expect confirmation of the job status at key points, particularly where delays exceed the original estimate. We will act to keep the repair moving, but we cannot guarantee a contractor’s performance.

items.title: chasing a contractor for repairs
items.content: If repeated chasing does not resolve the issue, we may close the contractor instruction and arrange for the remaining work to be reassessed. Any decision will take account of the nature of the damage, the age of the claim and the availability of suitable trades. The member will be notified before any material change is made.

items.title: chasing a contractor for repairs
items.content: If a repair contractor has been instructed but has not attended within the agreed timescale, you may contact our claims team so we can chase the appointment on your behalf. Please have your claim reference to hand when you call. We will record any delay and update you on the next available step.

items.title: chasing a contractor for repairs
items.content: Where repairs are being managed by one of our approved contractors, we expect the contractor to keep you informed of progress and to arrange access with you directly. If you have not heard from them, please tell us as soon as possible. We will contact the contractor and ask for an update.

items.title: chasing a contractor for repairs
items.content: You should not arrange replacement work or chase a contractor privately unless we have confirmed that this is your responsibility under the claim. If the contractor has missed an appointment, we may ask you for the date, time and any messages received. This helps us follow up the matter promptly.

items.title: chasing a contractor for repairs
items.content: When repair work is delayed, we may seek a revised completion date from the contractor and monitor the case until the work is finished. If further delay is caused by parts, weather or access issues, we will explain this where known. We will not close the repair file while a live contractor issue remains unresolved.

items.title: temporary accommodation during repairs
items.content: Where a claim for insured damage makes your home unfit to live in, we may arrange temporary accommodation for you and your household while essential repairs are carried out. The accommodation must be reasonably similar to your normal standard of living and suitable for your immediate needs.

items.title: temporary accommodation during repairs
items.content: Temporary accommodation is provided only for the period reasonably required to make the home habitable again. We will review the likely repair time with our appointed contractor and may ask for updates where delays occur.

items.title: temporary accommodation during repairs
items.content: If you cannot remain in the property because of an insured event, we may pay reasonable additional living expenses linked to the move. This can include necessary accommodation costs, subject to the terms, conditions and limits of your policy.

items.title: temporary accommodation during repairs
items.content: We will not usually provide temporary accommodation where the damage does not prevent safe occupation of the home. Minor works, cosmetic repairs and improvements are not normally covered under this section.

items.title: temporary accommodation during repairs
items.content: Any accommodation must be agreed with us in advance unless there is an immediate emergency. If you arrange accommodation without our consent, we may only consider the cost we would otherwise have incurred.

items.title: temporary accommodation during repairs
items.content: Temporary accommodation cover may extend to pets where suitable arrangements are reasonably necessary and agreed by us. However, we do not pay for luxury facilities or costs unrelated to the insured loss.

items.title: temporary accommodation during repairs
items.content: If alternative accommodation is required, you must take reasonable steps to reduce the cost and avoid unnecessary delay. We may ask you to consider comparable options within a practical distance from your home, school or workplace.

items.title: a mortgage application waiting on payslips
items.content: Where a mortgage application is awaiting recent payslips, the application shall remain in a pending status until the documents are received and checked. We may be unable to issue a final decision or proceed to offer stage without satisfactory evidence of income.

items.title: a mortgage application waiting on payslips
